diseases.summary: Periods that bring on far more blood than usual, or that drag on for many days, can make daily life hard and leave a person worn out. It happens most often when an egg isn't released in a cycle, which lowers progesterone, or when the uterus has growths such as fibroids or polyps. Anyone whose bleeding soaks through protection every hour or who notices bleeding between periods should contact a clinician.

diseases.name: Hemangioblastoma
diseases.summary: A hemangioblastoma is a slow-growing, noncancerous tumor of the blood-vessel-forming cells in the brain, spinal cord, or retina. Its symptoms depend on where it develops and whether the tumor or its fluid-filled cysts press on nearby nerve tissue. It is most often linked to the inherited von Hippel-Lindau disease, though many cases occur with no known cause.

diseases.name: Hemangioma
diseases.summary: A benign vascular birthmark that usually shows up in the first weeks of life and is typically harmless. Most of these marks fade on their own over the first decade, so treatment is needed only when they interfere with vision, breathing, or other vital functions, or sit in a cosmetically sensitive spot.

diseases.name: Hemifacial spasm
diseases.summary: A nerve-related movement disorder in which twitching or involuntary contractions affect the muscles on one side of the face, typically starting around the eye. The episodes can spread over time and are not dangerous, though they can be bothersome and socially awkward. A blood vessel pressing on the facial nerve is the usual underlying cause.

symptoms.name: spasms on both sides of face

diseases.name: Hemochromatosis
diseases.summary: Hemochromatosis is an inherited disorder in which the gut absorbs more iron than the body needs, and the surplus accumulates in organs such as the liver, heart, and pancreas. Many people never notice symptoms, and when they do, the early signs are vague and easily mistaken for other conditions. Left untreated, the iron buildup can progress to liver disease, heart problems, and diabetes.

diseases.name: Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS)
diseases.summary: This is a serious blood-clotting disorder in which tiny vessels become inflamed and clots form throughout the body, often injuring the kidneys. It most often follows a gut infection with a particular strain of E. coli and strikes mainly young children. With prompt treatment, most people, especially children, recover fully.

diseases.name: Hemophilia
diseases.summary: Hemophilia is an inherited condition in which the blood cannot form clots well because of a shortage of specific clotting proteins. Bleeding can be prolonged after injuries or procedures, and the most dangerous complication is bleeding inside the body, especially into the brain. It is treated mainly by replacing the missing clotting factor, with newer non-factor therapies also available.

diseases.name: Hemorrhoids
diseases.summary: Hemorrhoids are clusters of enlarged blood vessels in the anal canal and lower rectum that can sit inside or just under the skin near the anus. They are often linked to straining, pregnancy, and aging, and most cases improve with self-care. Bleeding or persistent symptoms still warrant a medical check to rule out more serious causes.

diseases.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
diseases.summary: A condition in which a failing liver lets toxins, especially ammonia, build up in the blood and disturb brain function. It can progress from attention and sleep problems to confusion and coma if not treated promptly. It is most often linked to advanced liver scarring, though acute liver failure, portal blood flow bypassing the liver, alcohol use, and certain medicines can also trigger it.

diseases.name: Hepatitis A
diseases.summary: This liver infection spreads mainly through contaminated food or water and close contact with an infected person. Many people who catch it have no symptoms, and those who do usually recover fully within weeks to months. Prevention relies on handwashing and vaccination.

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.summary: A viral infection of the liver that most adults clear fully, though in some people it lingers for years and can lead to scarring, liver failure, or cancer. Early signs often appear weeks to months after exposure, and some people, especially young children, have no noticeable symptoms. A vaccine offers reliable prevention, and prompt treatment after exposure can lower the chance of infection.

diseases.name: Hepatitis C
diseases.summary: Hepatitis C is a long-lasting viral infection that inflames and can gradually scar the liver, and it spreads through contact with infected blood. Many people carry it for years without noticing anything, so screening is recommended for most adults. Modern antiviral drugs cure the infection in most cases.

diseases.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
diseases.summary: This cancer starts in the liver's main cell type and most often develops in people already living with long-term liver scarring from hepatitis B or C. It usually causes no early warning signs, so it is often found through screening or only after it has advanced. People with a known risk who notice unexplained changes should be seen by a clinician promptly.

diseases.name: Hepatopulmonary syndrome
diseases.summary: Liver disease that has become advanced can cause tiny lung blood vessels to widen, so less oxygen passes from the lungs into the blood. Breathlessness is typically the first sign, often worse upright and easing when lying down. Liver transplantation is the only treatment that reverses the lung problem, while oxygen can partly help in the meantime.

diseases.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
diseases.summary: A genetic disorder that runs in families, where abnormal direct connections form between arteries and veins in places like the skin, nose, gut, lungs, brain, and liver. These fragile connections can grow over time and bleed, and the degree of illness varies widely even among relatives. Frequent nosebleeds and small red spots on the skin are typical early signs.

diseases.name: Herniated disk
diseases.summary: A slipped or ruptured spinal disk occurs when the soft inner core of a cushion between vertebrae pushes through a tear in its tougher outer shell. Most often in the lower back and less often in the neck, it tends to irritate a nearby nerve, producing pain, tingling or weakness usually on one side of the body. Many people with this problem have no symptoms at all.

diseases.name: Hiatal hernia
diseases.summary: A hiatal hernia happens when part of the stomach pushes upward through the muscular opening in the diaphragm into the chest. Small ones often go unnoticed, while larger ones can let stomach contents rise into the food pipe and cause reflux-type discomfort. Most people are managed with lifestyle changes or medication, and surgery is reserved for very large cases.

diseases.name: Hiccups
diseases.summary: Hiccups are involuntary contractions of the muscle under the lungs that briefly snap the voice box shut, producing a distinctive sound. Most episodes fade within minutes and are often set off by large meals, fizzy or alcoholic drinks, or sudden strong emotion. Episodes lasting longer than two days, or ones that interfere with eating, sleep, or breathing, call for a medical visit.

diseases.name: Hidradenitis suppurativa
diseases.summary: A long-lasting skin disorder that forms pus-filled bumps in folds and friction-prone areas, usually beginning in early adulthood. Over time the bumps can return, connect into underground channels, and leave scars. Seeing a skin specialist early helps control flares and limit lasting damage.

diseases.name: High cholesterol
diseases.summary: Elevated fat-like particles in the bloodstream can gradually build up inside arteries, narrowing them and raising the chance of heart attack or stroke. The condition usually produces no warning signs, so a blood test is the only reliable way to detect it. Diet, activity, weight, smoking, and alcohol all influence it, and it can also run in families.

diseases.name: Hilar cholangiocarcinoma
diseases.summary: This cancer begins in the cells lining the point where the two main channels leaving the liver merge, interrupting the flow of digestive fluid. Because it often grows quietly, early signs are subtle, and blockage usually shows up as yellowing, itching, or changes in urine and stool color. It is the most common form of bile duct cancer yet still uncommon overall.

diseases.name: Hip dysplasia
diseases.summary: Hip dysplasia is a condition in which the hip socket does not fully cover the ball of the thighbone, so the joint can partly or fully slip out of place. It is usually present from birth, and early detection often allows a simple brace to correct it. If it goes unnoticed, it can later cause wear, cartilage injury, and groin pain in adolescence or adulthood.

diseases.name: HIV/AIDS
diseases.summary: HIV is a virus that gradually weakens the immune system, and without treatment it can progress to AIDS. Early on, many people feel flu-like, and later the body struggles to fight off infections. Modern medicine keeps the virus under control in most people, so the infection rarely advances to AIDS.

diseases.name: Hives and angioedema
diseases.summary: Hives are itchy, raised welts on the skin that are usually brief and harmless, while angioedema is a deeper swelling that often shows up around the face and lips. Both are usually treated with antihistamines and tend to resolve on their own, though swelling of the throat or tongue can block the airway and needs emergency care.

diseases.name: Hoarding disorder
diseases.summary: This mental health condition causes a person to hold onto belongings compulsively, even when they have little value, until living areas fill up and become hard to move through or use. People often feel strong attachment to their things and may not recognize the situation as a problem. It typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood and tends to worsen with age.

diseases.name: Hodgkin lymphoma (Hodgkin disease)
diseases.summary: A cancer of the lymph system's white blood cells that often shows up first as painless swelling in the neck, armpits, or groin. It mainly affects young adults and people over 65, and it responds well to treatment, with many cases curable.

diseases.name: Huntington's disease
diseases.summary: A hereditary brain disorder that gradually impairs movement, thinking, and emotional health, most often becoming noticeable in middle adulthood. Each child of an affected parent has an even chance of inheriting the responsible gene. Medications can ease some symptoms, but they cannot stop the progressive decline.

diseases.name: Hydrocele
diseases.summary: A hydrocele is a fluid-filled enlargement around a testicle that makes the scrotum look swollen. It is usually present from birth and frequently disappears during infancy, while in older males it can follow an injury, inflammation, or infection. It is typically painless and harmless, but a medical check is still needed to rule out more serious causes.

diseases.name: Hydrocephalus
diseases.summary: Hydrocephalus is a condition where excess fluid collects in the brain's internal chambers, enlarging them and raising pressure that can injure brain tissue. Its signs differ with age, ranging from a swollen head in babies to memory, walking, and bladder problems in older adults. Some infant symptoms, such as seizures or repeated vomiting, require emergency care.

diseases.name: Hydronephrosis
diseases.summary: A condition where urine backs up into one or both kidneys because it cannot drain properly, usually from a blockage in the urinary tract or a birth difference. Many people have no noticeable signs, but when they do, pain, urinary changes, and general illness are the typical complaints. Long-standing cases can damage the kidney, so timely evaluation matters.

diseases.name: Hypercalcemia
diseases.summary: Excess calcium in the blood often arises when the parathyroid glands overproduce their hormone, though cancer, some medications, and high calcium or vitamin D supplements can also be responsible. Many people have no noticeable signs when the elevation is mild, while more significant cases can affect the kidneys, digestion, bones, muscles, brain, and heart. Seeing a doctor promptly is advisable if thirst, frequent urination, or stomach pain develops.

diseases.name: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon blood disorder in which a persistent surplus of one kind of immune cell injures tissues such as the skin, lungs, gut, heart, or nerves. Which symptoms appear depends on which organs are affected. Treatment can target an underlying trigger when one exists and may also use medicines that bring the cell count down.

diseases.name: Hyperhidrosis
diseases.summary: Hyperhidrosis is a condition in which a person sweats far more than their surroundings, activity, or emotions would explain, sometimes enough to soak clothing or drip from the hands. It often disrupts daily life and can lead to embarrassment or social withdrawal. Treatment typically starts with stronger antiperspirants and can progress to medications, therapies, or surgery when needed.

diseases.name: Hyperoxaluria and oxalosis
diseases.summary: A condition where the urine carries too much of a naturally occurring chemical, usually from a gene change, an intestinal disorder, or a high-oxalate diet, and it often first shows up as a kidney stone. If the kidneys decline and oxalate builds up in the blood, it can deposit in blood vessels, bones, and organs, a state called oxalosis. Early detection and prompt treatment are important for protecting kidney health.

diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid)
diseases.summary: An overactive thyroid makes more hormone than the body needs, which speeds up metabolism and can cause unplanned weight loss, a racing or irregular heartbeat, and jitteriness. Symptoms can be easy to miss or mistake for other problems, especially in older adults. Treatment options include medications, radioactive iodine, or surgery, and some cases resolve on their own.

diseases.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
diseases.summary: A genetic thickening of the heart muscle, most often in the wall between the heart's chambers, can make it harder for the heart to pump. Many carriers never notice anything, while a minority develop breathing trouble, chest discomfort, or fainting, and some are at risk of dangerous rhythm problems. Because it runs in families, relatives are typically advised to get screened.

diseases.name: Hypoglycemia
diseases.summary: Low blood sugar can cause a range of symptoms, from shakiness and sweating to confusion and, when severe, fainting or seizures. It is most often linked to diabetes treatment, though it can also occur in people without diabetes due to certain medicines, skipped meals, heavy drinking, or other medical conditions. Prompt intake of fast-acting sugar is the usual first step, and medical help is needed if symptoms persist or recur.

diseases.name: Hyponatremia
diseases.summary: Hyponatremia means the sodium concentration in the blood has dropped below normal, usually because the blood has been diluted by excess water or by an underlying illness. As water shifts into cells, they can swell, which may affect the brain and other organs. Mild cases may only need reduced fluid intake, while severe cases can require hospital treatment with intravenous salt solutions.

diseases.name: Hypopituitarism
diseases.summary: Hypopituitarism happens when the pituitary gland in the brain fails to produce enough of one or more of its hormones, which can disrupt growth, reproduction, thyroid function, stress response, and fluid balance. Symptoms often build slowly over months or years, though they can appear abruptly, and depend on which hormones are lacking. Treatment usually involves lifelong hormone replacement, and sudden symptoms with headache or vision changes need urgent care.

diseases.name: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome
diseases.summary: A heart defect present from birth leaves the left ventricle underdeveloped, so it cannot move enough blood, and the right side has to supply both the lungs and the body. Newborns with this problem typically become critically ill within the first days of life, and early recognition and treatment have substantially improved survival.

diseases.name: Hypospadias
diseases.summary: A birth difference in which the urethral opening sits on the underside of the penis rather than at its tip, usually noticed right after delivery. It is common, does not usually make caring for a baby difficult, and surgical repair typically restores normal appearance and urination, with fertility generally preserved.

diseases.name: Hypothermia
diseases.summary: When the body cools faster than it can generate warmth, the core temperature falls well below normal and organs start to slow down. Shaking is often the first sign, and it can progress to muddled thinking, poor coordination, and unconsciousness. Because affected people often fail to recognize their own decline, this needs prompt emergency help.

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid)
diseases.summary: This condition slows the body's metabolism because the small gland at the front of the neck produces too little of its key hormone. Symptoms often creep in over years and are easy to mistake for ordinary aging or tiredness. A simple blood test confirms it, and daily hormone replacement tablets generally bring it under control.

diseases.name: Idiopathic hypersomnia
diseases.summary: This is a lasting sleep disorder in which people feel excessively drowsy through the day even after long nights of sleep. Getting up is hard, and people may feel disoriented afterward, while naps rarely bring real rest. The cause is unknown, it usually begins in youth, and sudden urges to sleep can be dangerous during activities like driving.

diseases.name: IgA nephropathy (Berger disease)
diseases.summary: This kidney disorder occurs when an immune protein accumulates in the kidney filters and triggers ongoing irritation that slowly reduces their filtering ability. Many people have few or no signs for years, and it is often found incidentally through urine testing. Progression varies widely, and while there is no cure, treatments and blood pressure control can slow it down.

diseases.name: Illness anxiety disorder
diseases.summary: A long-lasting condition where a person becomes fixated on the belief that they have, or will develop, a serious disease, often after noticing ordinary body sensations or minor changes. The fear persists even when medical checks find nothing serious, and it can strongly disrupt daily life. Counseling and sometimes medication can ease it.

diseases.name: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
diseases.summary: A blood disorder in which the immune system destroys platelets, leaving the body with too few to clot properly. It typically shows up as bruises and small reddish-purple spots on the skin, along with bleeding from the gums, nose, or other places. It is more often seen in young women and can last for years in adults, while children often recover on their own.

diseases.name: Impacted wisdom teeth
diseases.summary: Wisdom teeth that get stuck under the gum line, often because there is no room for them to come through, frequently cause no trouble at all. When they do, the trouble tends to involve the gums and jaw, and they can also lead to decay or damage to neighboring teeth. Pain or problems usually lead to removal, though some dentists suggest removing them preventively.

diseases.name: Incompetent cervix
diseases.summary: A weakened cervix can open too early during pregnancy, which may lead to late loss or preterm delivery. Often there are no warning signs, but some people notice pressure, cramps, or light bleeding, usually before the 24th week. Treatments such as a stitch placed around the cervix, medication, and ultrasound monitoring are used when the problem is identified.

diseases.name: Indigestion
diseases.summary: Indigestion is discomfort or pain in the upper belly that can feel like burning, fullness, or bloating, and it often has no identifiable underlying cause. It tends to come and go and is frequently managed through diet changes, lifestyle adjustments, and sometimes medication. Most mild cases are harmless, but persistent symptoms or warning signs such as weight loss, black stools, or chest pain need prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Infant reflux
diseases.summary: Spitting up after feeds is very common in babies and usually harmless when the infant is content and gaining weight. It tends to fade by around 18 months. Specific warning signs, such as poor weight gain, forceful vomiting, or blood or green fluid, call for prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Infertility
diseases.summary: Infertility is the inability to conceive after a year or more of regular unprotected intercourse, and it can stem from one partner, both, or a combination of factors. Many people find that medical treatments improve their chances of having a child. Most cases show no signs apart from not becoming pregnant, though some people have menstrual irregularities or hormone-related changes.

diseases.name: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
diseases.summary: Inflammatory bowel disease is a long-term condition in which the digestive tract becomes chronically inflamed. Its symptoms depend on which part of the gut is involved and how intense the inflammation is. With ongoing specialist care and consistent treatment, many people can keep symptoms under control for extended periods.

diseases.name: Inflammatory breast cancer
diseases.summary: This is an aggressive form of breast cancer that tends to swell the breast and change the skin's color and texture rather than forming a noticeable lump. It typically progresses over weeks to months and is often mistaken for a breast infection, so persistent changes warrant prompt medical evaluation with a tissue sample.

diseases.name: Influenza (flu)
diseases.summary: Influenza is a virus that infects the nose, throat, and lungs and usually spreads during winter months in each hemisphere. Most people recover at home, but it can occasionally lead to serious complications, especially in those with underlying health problems. Symptoms tend to appear quickly, a day or few after exposure.

diseases.name: Ingrown hair
diseases.summary: A hair that was cut or pulled out regrows and bends back into the skin, leading to small tender lumps that can sting or itch. It is most often seen in people with tightly coiled hair who shave closely. Usually it clears up by itself, but medical advice is worth seeking if it lingers or keeps coming back.

diseases.name: Inherited metabolic disorders
diseases.summary: A group of hundreds of genetic conditions in which a faulty gene disrupts the chemical reactions the body uses to produce energy or to build and clear substances. Depending on the type, harmful byproducts can accumulate or needed compounds can run short. Symptoms vary widely by the specific disorder and its severity.

diseases.name: Insomnia
diseases.summary: Insomnia is a widespread sleep problem in which falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking too early becomes a recurring struggle, leaving people unrefreshed. It often shows up as daytime fatigue, irritability, and trouble concentrating, and it is considered chronic when it persists for three months or longer. Many cases improve with changes to daily routines, but a doctor should be consulted when it interferes with everyday functioning.

diseases.name: Insulinoma
diseases.summary: A rare pancreatic tumor that keeps releasing insulin even when blood sugar is already dropping, causing repeated episodes of dangerously low glucose. Most cases are non-cancerous and surgery often cures them, though severe lows can affect the brain and need urgent care.

diseases.name: Intermittent explosive disorder
diseases.summary: This is a long-term condition where a person has repeated, sudden episodes of rage or violence that are far out of proportion to what triggered them. The episodes come and go, often with little warning, and can strain relationships, work, school, and even bring legal trouble. Treatment typically combines talk therapy with medication aimed at controlling impulsive aggression.

diseases.name: Interstitial lung disease
diseases.summary: Interstitial lung disease is an umbrella term for many conditions in which the lung tissue becomes inflamed and then scarred, leaving it stiff and less able to expand and move oxygen into the blood. Breathlessness, especially during exertion, and a persistent dry cough are typical, and the scarring is usually permanent. Treatment aims to slow further damage and ease symptoms, since many causes exist and the course is hard to predict.

diseases.name: Intestinal ischemia
diseases.summary: When blood supply to the bowel drops because an artery is blocked or pressure falls, the gut tissue starves for oxygen. This can come on suddenly as an emergency or build slowly over weeks to months. Older adults and people with narrowed arteries or heart rhythm problems are at greatest risk.

diseases.name: Intracranial hematoma
diseases.summary: Bleeding inside the skull can press on brain tissue and worsen over hours to weeks, sometimes after a period with no obvious signs. It is often triggered by a burst vessel or a head blow and is life-threatening, typically needing urgent surgical or medical treatment. Anyone with head trauma who becomes drowsy, confused, or vomits should seek emergency care right away.

diseases.name: Intracranial venous malformations
diseases.summary: Intracranial venous malformations are enlarged veins within the brain that usually cause no problems. Many people never learn they have one, and it is often discovered incidentally on a scan done for something else. When symptoms do appear, they are typically neurological and warrant a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN)
diseases.summary: This is a noncancerous growth in the pancreas's duct system that often causes no problems and is frequently found by accident on scans. Most cases are managed by watching them over time, with surgery reserved for higher-risk lesions. Age, smoking, diabetes, and long-standing pancreas inflammation are linked to a greater chance of developing one.

diseases.name: Invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC)
diseases.summary: This cancer begins in the milk ducts of the breast and, once it breaks through the duct wall into surrounding tissue, can reach lymph nodes and other organs. It is the most frequent form of breast cancer and often shows up as a lump, though it sometimes produces no symptoms and is found on a screening mammogram first. Any new breast lump or skin or nipple change warrants a prompt visit to a clinician.

diseases.name: Invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC)
diseases.summary: This cancer begins in the milk-producing lobules of the breast and spreads into surrounding tissue, often without forming a distinct lump. Because it tends to present as thickening or subtle skin and nipple changes, it is frequently detected later than other breast cancers. Any new breast change warrants prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Iritis
diseases.summary: Iritis is swelling of the colored ring around the pupil, usually in one eye, and it can begin abruptly and worsen quickly. It is the most frequent form of uveitis and can appear at any age. Infections, injuries, and autoimmune disorders can trigger it, though often no cause is found, and prompt specialist assessment helps protect vision.

diseases.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
diseases.summary: Irritable bowel syndrome is a long-lasting digestive disorder in which the gut appears normal on examination but muscle contractions and nerve sensitivity cause pain and changes in bowel movements. Its symptoms tend to recur over months or years. Dietary changes, stress reduction, and lifestyle adjustments often help, and severe cases may respond to medication or counseling.

diseases.name: Ischemic colitis
diseases.summary: A condition where a section of the large intestine receives too little blood, so its tissue becomes starved of oxygen, swollen and damaged. It often causes belly pain on the left side and bloody stools, and most cases get better without specialized treatment. Older adults and people with blood vessel or circulation problems are the most affected.

diseases.name: Itchy skin (pruritus)
diseases.summary: Itch without a visible rash is a sensation that prompts scratching and is often linked to dry skin, becoming more frequent with age. It can stay localized or spread across the body, and repeated scratching can thicken or inflame the skin. Lasting relief depends on finding the underlying trigger, while moisturizers and gentle care help in the meantime.

diseases.name: Jaw cancer
diseases.summary: Jaw cancer is an umbrella term for several different malignancies that start in the jawbone or nearby oral tissues, or spread into the jaw from neighboring areas. The signs a person notices depend on where the growth began and which structures it presses on or invades. Because benign growths in this area can cause similar problems, any persistent mouth sore, jaw lump, or loosening teeth should be checked by a clinician.

diseases.name: Jaw tumors and cysts
diseases.summary: A group of uncommon, mostly noncancerous growths and fluid-filled sacs can form in the jawbone or nearby soft tissue, and many cause no noticeable signs at all. When they do cause trouble, they may swell the jaw, loosen or displace teeth, or slowly erode bone. Dental X-rays are often how they are first found, and treatment is usually surgical.

diseases.name: Jellyfish stings
diseases.summary: Stings from jellyfish usually cause immediate burning pain and marks on the skin that can be itchy and swollen. In uncommon cases the venom spreads through the body and causes nausea, headache, or breathing trouble, which needs emergency care. Most minor stings settle within days to weeks with simple home care.

diseases.name: Jet lag disorder
diseases.summary: Jet lag is a short-term disruption to the body's internal clock that appears after rapid travel across several time zones. Eastward trips and crossing more zones tend to make it worse, and older adults usually need longer to bounce back. Most people recover on their own, but frequent travelers may benefit from a sleep specialist's input.

diseases.name: Jock itch
diseases.summary: A fungal skin infection that brings an irritating, ring-like patch to the groin and upper inner thighs. It is more frequent in young men and people who sweat heavily, and it usually resolves within a few weeks with over-the-counter antifungal treatment.

diseases.name: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA)
diseases.summary: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis is the most frequent form of joint inflammation in children under 16, arising when an overactive immune system attacks the joints without a known trigger. It can cause ongoing joint discomfort and swelling that may fade within a few years or persist into adulthood. Prompt evaluation matters because untreated inflammation can permanently damage joints.

diseases.name: Kaposi sarcoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare form of skin-based cancer that starts in the cells lining blood and lymph vessels and is driven by a common herpesvirus. It typically shows up as colored patches or raised spots on the skin, most often on the face and limbs, and it can spread to internal organs in advanced cases. Risk is highest in people with weakened immune systems, such as those with HIV or transplant recipients on immune-suppressing drugs.

diseases.name: Kawasaki disease
diseases.summary: A childhood inflammatory illness that affects medium-sized blood vessels, especially the arteries that feed the heart. It usually begins with a prolonged high fever along with changes to the skin, eyes, mouth, and lymph glands. Quick treatment greatly reduces the chance of lasting heart problems.

diseases.name: Keloid scar
diseases.summary: A keloid is an overgrown scar that develops after the skin has been damaged and extends beyond the original wound. It is more likely in people with darker skin, in those under 30, and in people with a family history. It is not dangerous, but it can cause itching or discomfort and may return after treatment.

diseases.name: Keratitis
diseases.summary: Keratitis is swelling or irritation of the clear front layer of the eye. It can be triggered by an injury or by bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites, and contact lens misuse is a notable contributor. Prompt evaluation by an eye specialist usually prevents lasting vision loss.

diseases.name: Keratoconus
diseases.summary: A progressive eye disorder in which the cornea gradually thins and bulges into a cone, distorting sight. It usually starts in the late teens to thirties and can advance slowly over a decade or more. Early changes are often manageable with glasses or contact lenses, while later stages may need specialized lenses or surgery.

diseases.name: Keratosis pilaris
diseases.summary: A harmless, long-lasting skin pattern that leaves small rough bumps on areas like the arms and thighs, usually without discomfort. It tends to be worse when the air is dry and often fades on its own by adulthood. Because it is so widespread and mostly cosmetic, treatment is typically optional.

diseases.name: Kidney cancer
diseases.summary: Kidney cancer often causes no noticeable signs in its early stages, and symptoms that do appear tend to be blood in the urine, flank or back discomfort, fatigue, and unintended weight loss. Most cases are renal cell carcinoma, and the disease is more frequent in men and in people of older age. Anyone with persistent or worrying symptoms should arrange a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Kidney cysts
diseases.summary: Small fluid-filled sacs that form on or inside the kidneys are usually harmless and are often discovered by accident during scans done for other reasons. Most people never notice them, and they rarely affect how the kidneys work. Symptoms appear mainly when a sac gets large or becomes infected.

diseases.name: Kidney infection
diseases.summary: A kidney infection is a bacterial infection that starts in the lower urinary tract and climbs up into one or both kidneys. It typically brings fever, discomfort when passing urine, and pain in the back or side, and it can cause lasting kidney injury or a dangerous bloodstream infection if left untreated.

diseases.name: Kidney stones
diseases.summary: Small crystal-like clumps can form inside the kidneys and, once they move into the thin tubes leading to the bladder, may block urine flow and cause intense waves of discomfort. Many people first notice them through flank or lower belly pain combined with changes in urination. Medical evaluation is advisable promptly, particularly when fever or an inability to pass urine is present.

diseases.name: Kleptomania
diseases.summary: Kleptomania is a psychological condition in which a person feels a strong, hard-to-resist pull to take things they have no real use for and could easily pay for. Stealing brings a brief sense of relief, which is typically followed by guilt and shame, and the cycle tends to repeat. It is uncommon and usually responds to medication or therapy aimed at managing the urges.

diseases.name: Klinefelter syndrome
diseases.summary: A genetic variation where a person assigned male at birth carries an extra X chromosome. It often goes unnoticed until adolescence or adulthood, when reduced testosterone, smaller testicles, or fertility problems prompt evaluation. Effects range from barely noticeable to clearly visible, and many people only learn of it when trying to have children.

diseases.name: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
diseases.summary: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome is an uncommon condition present from birth that affects the blood vessels, skin, soft tissues, bones, and lymph vessels, usually on one leg. It typically shows up as a colored skin mark along with abnormal veins and extra growth of a limb. Because it is usually recognized in infancy, prompt diagnosis and ongoing care are important to manage symptoms and reduce complications.

diseases.name: Knee bursitis
diseases.summary: Knee bursitis is when one of the small fluid-filled cushions near the knee becomes swollen and irritated, most often the one over the kneecap or on the inner side below the joint. It tends to build up gradually from repeated pressure or friction, though a hard blow can bring it on suddenly. Warmth, tenderness, and swelling are the typical signs, and an infection can occasionally develop, which calls for prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Knee pain
diseases.summary: Pain in the knee can come from an injury to the ligaments or cartilage, or from conditions such as arthritis, gout, or infection. Many mild cases improve with home care, while swelling, instability, or an inability to straighten the joint call for prompt medical review.

diseases.name: Kyphosis
diseases.summary: Kyphosis is an exaggerated forward curve of the upper spine. It often develops with age as bones weaken and compress, but it can also appear in children or teens due to spinal structure differences. Mild cases usually go unnoticed, while more pronounced curves can hurt and change posture.

diseases.name: Latex allergy
diseases.summary: Latex allergy is an immune overreaction to proteins in natural rubber, so the body treats latex as a threat. Reactions range from skin irritation to, rarely, a life-threatening whole-body response. People with frequent exposure to latex, such as healthcare workers and those with spina bifida, face the highest risk.

diseases.name: Left ventricular hypertrophy
diseases.summary: Left ventricular hypertrophy means the muscular wall of the heart's left ventricle has grown thicker and stiffer, which makes it harder for the organ to fill and push out blood. It develops slowly, most often because of long-standing high blood pressure, and usually causes no noticeable signs at first. Over time it can lead to irregular heartbeats and heart failure, so people at risk benefit from routine heart monitoring.

diseases.name: Left-sided heart failure
diseases.summary: When the left ventricle loses its ability to pump or fill properly, blood backs up into the lungs and pressure rises on that side of the heart. Long-standing problems such as high blood pressure and narrowed heart arteries are common reasons it develops. Although treatment and lifestyle changes can help, the condition can become life-threatening and needs prompt medical attention when symptoms worsen.

diseases.name: Legg-Calve-Perthes disease
diseases.summary: A childhood hip disorder in which blood flow to the rounded top of the thigh bone is briefly cut off, so that part of the bone dies and later collapses before healing. Children typically limp and feel ache in the hip, groin, thigh, or knee that gets worse with use. It usually affects one hip at a time and is much more frequent in boys.

diseases.name: Leiomyosarcoma (LMS)
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer that begins in smooth muscle tissue, which can occur in places such as the uterus, abdomen, limbs, or blood vessels. Its presentation and outlook depend heavily on where it starts, how far it has grown, and whether it can be removed surgically. Many cases first show up as a lump or as abdominal or pelvic discomfort.

diseases.name: Leukemia
diseases.summary: This blood cancer begins in the marrow and lymphatic tissue, where cells that normally fight infection multiply abnormally and fail to work properly. Its signs are often vague and easily mistaken for the flu or other routine illnesses, and it is sometimes found incidentally during blood work ordered for something else. Anyone with persistent, worrying symptoms should see a doctor promptly for evaluation.

diseases.name: Leukoplakia
diseases.summary: A condition where thick, whitish patches form on the soft tissues inside the mouth and cannot be wiped away. It is most often linked to long-term tobacco or alcohol irritation, and while most patches are harmless, some can harbor early cancer changes. A dentist or doctor should evaluate any mouth patch or sore that persists.

diseases.name: Lewy body dementia
diseases.summary: Lewy body dementia is a progressive brain disorder caused by abnormal protein clumps in nerve cells, and it is the second most common dementia after Alzheimer's. It impairs thinking and memory while also producing Parkinson-like movement problems, and it often brings vivid hallucinations and fluctuating alertness. Risk rises with age past sixty, is somewhat higher in men, and is greater for those with affected relatives.

diseases.name: Li-Fraumeni syndrome
diseases.summary: This is an inherited condition caused by a faulty copy of a gene that normally guards against damaged cells turning cancerous, so affected people face a much higher chance of several cancers, often at younger ages and sometimes more than once. The condition itself is not felt directly; the signs people notice come from whichever cancer develops, such as bone pain, a breast lump, or headaches. Regular screening and check-ups are the main way to catch these cancers early.

diseases.name: Lice
diseases.summary: Lice are tiny wingless insects that live on people and survive by taking blood, most often on the scalp in children. Their eggs cling to the hair and can resemble dandruff, and the infestation usually goes away with routine treatment. Most affected people can manage it at home without a medical visit.

diseases.name: Lichen planus
diseases.summary: A skin, hair, nail, mouth, and genital condition that makes flat, shiny, itchy bumps and lacy white patches inside the mouth, often in middle-aged adults. Many mild skin cases clear without treatment, while painful or intensely itchy cases may need prescription medication. Prompt evaluation helps rule out other conditions that cause similar sores and pain.

diseases.name: Lichen sclerosus
diseases.summary: A long-term skin disorder that leaves patches of skin looking pale or blotchy and thinner than usual, most often in the genital and anal region. It is not passed between people, and it tends to flare back even after it has been treated, so regular check-ups matter.

diseases.name: Lip cancer
diseases.summary: Lip cancer is a growth of abnormal cells in the skin of the lips, most often on the lower lip and usually a type called squamous cell carcinoma. It is tied to long sun exposure and tobacco use, and it often first shows up as a patch or sore that stays unhealed. Treatment is typically surgical removal, and small cases can often be taken out with minimal change to appearance.

diseases.name: Liposarcoma
diseases.summary: A cancer that begins in fat-storing cells and is classed among soft tissue sarcomas. It tends to form in the thigh, arm, or inside the abdomen, and it can be felt as a slowly enlarging mass. Surgical removal is the main treatment, sometimes combined with radiation.

diseases.name: Liver cancer
diseases.summary: Liver cancer that starts in the liver's own cells is a serious condition that often causes no noticeable warning signs early on. It is strongly tied to long-term liver damage from viral hepatitis, scarring, and fatty liver disease. Because symptoms tend to show up late, anyone with ongoing liver risk factors or worrying changes should see a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Liver disease
diseases.summary: Liver disease covers a range of conditions that interfere with the organ's jobs of processing nutrients, clearing waste, and producing blood-clotting proteins. It can be inherited or triggered by infections, heavy drinking, or excess body weight, and prolonged damage can progress to permanent scarring and organ failure. Many people have no obvious signs early on, so prompt evaluation gives the organ its best chance to recover.

diseases.name: Liver fibrosis
diseases.summary: Scarring of the liver builds up slowly after repeated injury, often from fatty liver disease, heavy drinking, or chronic viral hepatitis. Most people feel fine in early stages and only learn of it through routine blood work or imaging. Caught early and with the underlying cause treated, the scarring may stop progressing or partly reverse.

diseases.name: Long QT syndrome
diseases.summary: This heart rhythm disorder, which can be inherited or triggered later by certain medications, illnesses, or mineral imbalances, disrupts the heart's electrical timing and can cause sudden blackouts. Many affected people feel warning signs like lightheadedness or a racing pulse, while others have no symptoms and are found only on an electrocardiogram. Because it can lead to dangerous rhythms, anyone who faints or notices a pounding heartbeat should be evaluated promptly.

diseases.name: Low blood pressure (hypotension)
diseases.summary: Low blood pressure means the arteries are carrying less pressure than is typical for that person, often judged against a reading below roughly 90/60. Many people notice nothing, while others feel lightheaded, faint, or tired, especially after standing up or eating. A sudden or large drop can be dangerous, so finding the underlying cause matters.

diseases.name: Low sex drive in women
diseases.summary: Many women find their interest in sex goes up and down over the years, often alongside relationship changes, major life transitions such as pregnancy or menopause, illness, or certain medications. When reduced interest lasts or keeps coming back and causes distress, a clinician can look for treatable causes and suggest options. Lifestyle changes and, in some cases, medication can help.

diseases.name: Low sperm count
diseases.summary: Reduced sperm numbers in semen often produce no obvious warning signs, and the main way it shows up is difficulty conceiving after a year of regular unprotected intercourse. Some underlying causes bring along sexual, testicular, or hormonal symptoms that prompt an earlier medical visit. Lifestyle factors, illness, medications, and prior treatments can all contribute.

diseases.name: Lung cancer
diseases.summary: Lung cancer develops when cells in the lungs multiply abnormally and form a growth. Smoking is the biggest contributor, but people who have never smoked can also get it. It often causes no noticeable signs in its early stages, so symptoms usually appear once it has progressed.

diseases.name: Lupus nephritis
diseases.summary: This kidney condition arises when an autoimmune illness inflames the tiny filtering units of the kidneys, leading to leaking of blood cells and protein into urine and sometimes reduced kidney function. Its signs often show up as foamy urine, swelling in the lower body, and elevated blood pressure. Men and people of Black, Hispanic, or Asian descent are more affected by it than others.

diseases.name: Lyme disease
diseases.summary: Lyme disease is a bacterial infection passed on mainly through the bite of an infected tick. It tends to progress in stages, starting with a spreading rash and flu-like feelings and potentially reaching joints, nerves, and the heart if left untreated. Prompt medical attention after a possible tick exposure improves the chance of a good outcome.

diseases.name: Lymphedema
diseases.summary: Lymphedema is a buildup of protein-rich fluid in tissue that happens when the lymphatic drainage network is damaged or blocked, most often in an arm or leg. It is frequently a result of cancer treatments that remove or injure lymph nodes, though it can also run in families or appear without a clear cause. Persistent or worsening swelling warrants a doctor's visit, and any fever with redness or skin color change in the affected limb needs prompt attention because infection can develop.

diseases.name: Lymphoma
diseases.summary: Lymphoma is a group of blood cancers in which infection-fighting white cells multiply out of control and often form masses in lymph nodes. Many people first notice a painless lump, and the exact symptoms depend on the subtype and where it grows. Many forms respond well to modern therapy, so unexplained lumps or lasting systemic symptoms deserve prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Lynch syndrome
diseases.summary: Lynch syndrome is an inherited genetic change that raises the chance of several cancers, most notably colorectal and endometrial cancer, often at younger ages than usual. Most people have no signs until a cancer forms, so routine screening is the main way it is caught early. Anyone with a close relative who has the condition should speak with a genetic counselor.

diseases.name: Male breast cancer
diseases.summary: Male breast cancer is an uncommon malignancy that develops from cells in the chest tissue of men, most often affecting those who are older. Because all people have some breast tissue, it can arise at any age, and treatment usually centers on surgical removal, sometimes with chemotherapy or radiation. Early signs are typically a painless lump, skin or nipple changes, or fluid discharge from the nipple.

diseases.name: Male infertility
diseases.summary: Male infertility is a condition in which a man's reproductive system contributes to a couple's failure to conceive despite regular intercourse over an extended period. Causes can involve sperm production, sperm movement, or obstructions in the reproductive tract, and may be linked to infections, injuries, medications, or general health and lifestyle factors. Because it often causes no other obvious signs, a clinician usually needs to evaluate it to find the cause and guide treatment.

diseases.name: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs)
diseases.summary: A rare cancer that begins in the protective outer layer of peripheral nerves and usually sits in deep tissue of the limbs or trunk. It can arise on its own or grow out of a noncancerous nerve tumor, and people with a genetic nerve condition face higher odds. Early signs tend to be a growing lump, changing feelings in the area, or pain and weakness.

diseases.name: Mantle cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: This blood and lymph cancer begins in the outer ring of B cells within lymph nodes and often spreads to other organs. It is uncommon overall and tends to appear in older adults, most often after age 60. Early on it frequently causes no noticeable problems, and when symptoms do appear they are usually painless lumps and general body-wide complaints.

diseases.name: Marfan syndrome
diseases.summary: Marfan syndrome is an inherited disorder that weakens the body's supportive tissue, often affecting the heart, eyes, bones, and blood vessels. Affected people frequently have a tall, slender build with unusually long limbs and fingers. The most serious danger involves the main artery leaving the heart, so care centers on blood pressure medication, regular monitoring, and often surgery.

diseases.name: Marginal zone lymphoma
diseases.summary: This cancer begins in the immune system's B cells and grows slowly, most often in lymph nodes, the spleen, the stomach, or other organs. What a person notices depends on where the disease sits, so it can show up as swelling, digestive upset, or organ-specific changes. It is most often diagnosed in people over 60.

diseases.name: Mastitis
diseases.summary: Breast inflammation that often involves a bacterial infection, most commonly seen in people who are breastfeeding. It can make one or both breasts swollen, tender, warm and reddish, sometimes with fever and a general sense of being unwell. Prompt medical evaluation is advisable when breast symptoms cause concern.

diseases.name: MCAD deficiency
diseases.summary: A lifelong inherited enzyme problem stops the body from converting certain fats into usable energy, so fasting, illness, or fever can trigger sudden crises with dangerously low blood sugar. Usually detected through newborn screening, it is well controlled with diet and prompt treatment during illness, but untreated cases can lead to liver damage and coma.

diseases.name: Median arcuate ligament syndrome (MALS)
diseases.summary: A fibrous strip near the top of the abdomen can squeeze the artery that supplies the stomach, spleen, and liver, along with the nearby nerve network. Nerve irritation is the main source of symptoms, which are often pain and digestive trouble around meals. Surgery to loosen the strip is the usual treatment.

diseases.name: Medication overuse headaches
diseases.summary: This is a headache that comes back because the medicine taken to stop it is being used too often. It typically shows up most days, often rousing someone from sleep, and eases only while the painkiller is active. The problem is most likely in people who already have recurring headaches such as migraine and who rely on over-the-counter or prescription pain relievers frequently.

diseases.name: Medulloblastoma
diseases.summary: A malignant tumor that begins in the cerebellum, the lower back part of the brain that governs balance and coordination, and is the most frequent cancerous brain tumor in children. It can block fluid flow and raise pressure inside the skull, so headaches, vomiting, and balance or vision problems are typical early warning signs. Anyone with persistent symptoms of this kind should see a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Melanoma
diseases.summary: Melanoma is a form of skin cancer arising from the pigment-producing cells in the skin, and it can also appear in the eyes or inside the body. Its first signs often involve an existing mole that changes in size, shape, or color, or a new unusual dark spot. Because it is treatable when caught early, any worrying skin change warrants prompt evaluation by a clinician.

diseases.name: Meniere's disease
diseases.summary: This inner-ear disorder causes episodes of spinning, hearing changes, and pressure or noise in one ear, and these episodes tend to recur with symptom-free stretches between them. Hearing can gradually decline over the years, though treatment can reduce how much the condition disrupts daily activities. It usually appears in middle age, and other conditions can produce similar symptoms, so a clinician should evaluate them.

diseases.name: Meningioma
diseases.summary: A meningioma is a growth arising from the protective membranes that wrap the brain and spinal cord rather than from brain tissue itself. Most are non-cancerous and expand slowly, so many never cause noticeable problems and are discovered incidentally on scans. Symptoms depend on which area the growth presses against, and warning signs such as a sudden seizure or a sudden severe headache require emergency evaluation.

diseases.name: Meningitis
diseases.summary: Meningitis is swelling of the protective layers surrounding the brain and spinal cord, usually caused by a virus but sometimes by bacteria, fungi, or parasites. Many cases resolve on their own, yet bacterial forms can progress quickly and need prompt antibiotic treatment. Anyone suspecting this condition should be assessed by a clinician without delay.

diseases.name: Menopause
diseases.summary: Menopause is the permanent end of menstruation, confirmed once a full year passes without a period. It is a natural life stage, usually reached in the late 40s or early 50s, and it is often preceded by a transition phase in which hormone shifts cause irregular cycles and bothersome symptoms. Lifestyle measures and medical treatments, including hormone therapy, can help manage these effects.

diseases.name: Mental illness
diseases.summary: Mental illness is an umbrella term for conditions that disturb a person's mood, thinking, or behavior, and it becomes a concern when persistent symptoms start to disrupt everyday functioning. Its warning signs can appear emotionally, cognitively, or as unexplained physical aches. Many people improve with a mix of medication and counseling, and seeking help early tends to prevent worsening.

diseases.name: Meralgia paresthetica
diseases.summary: This is a nerve irritation condition where a sensory nerve running down the outside of the upper thigh gets squeezed, leading to odd sensations and discomfort in that area. Tight clothing, extra body weight, pregnancy, and diabetes are typical contributors. Many people improve with looser clothing, though medication or surgery are options for persistent cases.

diseases.name: Merkel cell carcinoma
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon but aggressive skin cancer that usually shows up as a fast-growing bump on sun-exposed areas, most often the face, head, or neck. It is more often seen in older adults and in people with fair skin, sun exposure, or weakened immune systems. Because it can spread quickly, prompt medical evaluation of any new or changing skin bump is important.

diseases.name: Mesenteric ischemia
diseases.summary: Reduced blood flow to the small intestine can cause lasting harm, and the cause and timing determine how it shows up. A sudden, acute blockage typically brings intense belly pain with fever and vomiting and requires immediate surgical care. A slowly developing version tends to cause predictable pain after meals and can lead to weight loss.

diseases.name: Mesenteric lymphadenitis
diseases.summary: This is a condition where the lymph nodes that sit within the tissue anchoring the bowel to the abdominal wall become enlarged and irritated, most often after a gut infection. It mostly affects children and adolescents. Although it can mimic appendicitis or intussusception, it generally resolves without specific treatment.

diseases.name: Mesothelioma
diseases.summary: A rare and aggressive cancer that arises from the thin protective lining covering the lungs, abdomen, heart, or testicles, most often in the chest. It is closely linked to past exposure to asbestos and often shows up decades later. Treatments exist, but a cure is not available for many patients.

diseases.name: Metachromatic leukodystrophy
diseases.summary: A rare inherited disorder in which the body cannot clear a certain fat from the nervous system, so it accumulates and gradually strips away the protective coating around nerves. Problems appear at different ages depending on the form, and they tend to progress over time, affecting movement, speech, thinking, and vision. There is currently no cure, though early diagnosis can help manage some symptoms.

diseases.name: Metastatic (stage 4) bladder cancer
diseases.summary: Bladder cancer that has spread beyond the bladder to distant organs is considered advanced and generally cannot be cured, though treatment can slow its growth and ease symptoms. Spread most often reaches lymph nodes, bones, liver, lungs, or brain, and the signs depend on where the cancer has traveled. Medicines such as immunotherapy or chemotherapy are typically the starting point of care.

diseases.name: Metastatic (stage 4) breast cancer
diseases.summary: Cancer that began in the breast and has spread to distant organs such as bone, brain, lungs or liver. It often shows up after an earlier breast cancer returns, and while it usually cannot be cured, treatment can control it and extend life. Symptoms depend largely on which organs are affected.

diseases.name: Metastatic (stage 4) esophageal cancer
diseases.summary: This is an advanced cancer of the esophagus, the muscular tube connecting the throat to the stomach, that has spread beyond its original site. It cannot be cured, but treatments can control it, ease symptoms, and support quality of life. The most noticeable signs usually involve swallowing difficulty and unintended weight loss, with others depending on which organs the cancer has reached.

diseases.name: Metastatic (stage 4) pancreatic cancer
diseases.summary: Stage 4 pancreatic cancer means the disease has moved from the pancreas to other areas, most often the liver, the abdominal lining, or the lungs. Because it is usually found late, it is generally not curable, but treatment can slow progression and relieve symptoms. Warning signs include belly pain, weight loss, yellowing of the skin, and breathing problems.

diseases.name: Metastatic (stage 4) prostate cancer
diseases.summary: Advanced prostate cancer that has moved beyond the gland into other body areas, often in people previously treated for prostate cancer. It frequently causes no noticeable signs early on, but as it progresses it can bring fatigue, urinary changes, unexplained weight loss, and bone or pelvic pain. Treatment generally aims to slow progression rather than cure it.

diseases.name: Metastatic (stage 4) sarcoma
diseases.summary: Stage 4 sarcoma means the cancer started in bone or soft tissue and has spread to a distant organ, where it usually cannot be fully cured. Symptoms vary a great deal depending on the tumor type and on which organs are involved, and some people have none for a long time. Treatments such as chemotherapy, surgery, targeted drugs, immunotherapy, and radiation can slow disease and ease symptoms.

diseases.name: Metastatic (stage 4) stomach cancer
diseases.summary: Cancer that began in the stomach and has spread to distant organs is usually not curable, but treatment can shrink or hold back growth, ease discomfort, and extend life. The spread most often lands in the abdominal lining, the liver, or lymph nodes, and the body's signals depend on where it has reached. Doctors weigh the tumor's biology when choosing therapy.

diseases.name: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)
diseases.summary: This cancer has spread beyond the prostate and keeps growing even though hormone-lowering treatment no longer works. Many people have no symptoms early on and it is often found on routine blood or imaging tests. When symptoms do appear, they usually relate to urination, bone pain or fractures, weakness, or fatigue.

diseases.name: Microscopic colitis
diseases.summary: This is a bowel disorder in which the large intestine seems normal to the eye but shows abnormal tissue when examined under a microscope, leading to ongoing loose, non-bloody bowel movements. Its trigger is unknown, though it appears more often in older adults and in women. Medication is the main treatment, and adjustments to eating and daily habits can also ease symptoms.

diseases.name: Migraine
diseases.summary: Migraine is a recurring neurological condition with a strong hereditary component that causes intense head pain and can come with sensory and digestive disturbances. Attacks vary widely in how often they happen and how long they last, and many people also notice warning signs beforehand or feel drained afterward. Because it is often underdiagnosed, tracking attacks and discussing the pattern with a clinician is recommended.

diseases.name: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI)
diseases.summary: Mild cognitive impairment is an intermediate stage between normal age-related thinking changes and dementia, involving noticeable lapses in memory, language, or decision-making. Daily functioning stays intact, and some people remain stable or improve over time, though a portion go on to develop dementia.

diseases.name: Miscarriage
diseases.summary: A pregnancy that ends on its own before the midpoint of gestation is a common outcome, and it is often caused by problems with the embryo's development rather than the mother's care. Bleeding, cramping in the lower abdomen or back, and tissue passing from the vagina are the typical signs. Anyone with these symptoms should contact their care team promptly, because the same signs can occasionally point to a dangerous pregnancy outside the uterus.

diseases.name: Mitral valve disease
diseases.summary: This heart valve condition involves the mitral valve, which sits between the left upper and lower heart chambers, and it can leak backward or become narrowed. Many affected people feel nothing for years, while others notice tiredness, breathlessness, or an uneven heartbeat. Age, prior heart disease, certain infections, some medications, and chest radiation raise the chance of developing it.

diseases.name: Mitral valve regurgitation
diseases.summary: This is a heart valve problem in which the mitral valve, which sits between the left upper and lower chambers, lets some blood flow back where it should not. Many people have only mild effects for years, while a more serious case can strain the heart and lead to rhythm trouble or heart failure. A medical evaluation is needed to decide whether monitoring, medication, or a procedure is appropriate.

diseases.name: Mitral valve stenosis
diseases.summary: A narrowing of the valve between the heart's upper and lower left chambers slows blood entering the main pumping chamber. It often progresses over many years and may cause no symptoms at first. Breathlessness, tiredness, and irregular heartbeats are the typical complaints, and it can be triggered or worsened by exertion, pregnancy, or infection.

diseases.name: Mittelschmerz
diseases.summary: A brief, one-sided twinge in the lower abdomen that shows up around the middle of the monthly cycle, when an ovary releases an egg. It usually fades within minutes to hours and rarely calls for treatment. Pain that is severe, comes with nausea or fever, or lingers should be checked by a clinician, since other conditions can cause similar pelvic pain.

diseases.name: Molar pregnancy
diseases.summary: A rare pregnancy abnormality in which tissue that should become the placenta grows abnormally into fluid-filled clusters, and any embryo cannot survive. It often looks like a normal early pregnancy at first, but it needs prompt medical treatment because it can lead to serious complications, including a rare cancer.

diseases.name: Moles
diseases.summary: Moles are small, usually harmless skin growths made of clusters of pigment-producing cells, and most people develop between 10 and 45 of them over their lifetime. Their appearance can shift over the years, but a mole that becomes irregular, changes shape or color, grows, or starts to itch or bleed should be checked by a clinician because melanoma, though uncommon, is the concern.

diseases.name: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS)
diseases.summary: This is a blood-protein abnormality in which bone marrow plasma cells make a small amount of abnormal protein, but it does not cause organ damage. It is typically discovered incidentally on routine blood work, and it is not cancer, though it modestly raises the lifetime risk of related plasma cell disorders. Most affected people never develop problems and need only periodic monitoring.

diseases.name: Mood disorders
diseases.summary: Mood disorders mainly disrupt emotional state, with depression and bipolar disorder as the best-known forms. Depression causes lasting low mood and loss of interest, while bipolar disorder cycles between low periods and elevated, high-energy phases. Because these conditions can raise the risk of suicidal thoughts, getting professional help early is important.

diseases.name: Morning sickness
diseases.summary: Nausea and vomiting during pregnancy, which can occur at any hour and usually peaks in the first trimester. For most people it eases by mid-to-late second trimester, though a small number experience severe, prolonged symptoms that lead to dehydration or significant weight loss.

diseases.name: Morphea
diseases.summary: Morphea is an uncommon skin disorder in which hardened, discolored patches form, most often on the trunk. The skin in these areas becomes tight and loses flexibility, though it usually softens and fades over several years. Doctors recommend early evaluation to limit new patches and catch any deeper involvement.

diseases.name: Mosquito bites
diseases.summary: Mosquito bites produce itchy, raised welts that typically settle on their own within a few days. In some people, especially children, the reaction can be much larger and more swollen, and in rare cases mosquitoes transmit serious infections. Seek medical care if bites come with high fever, severe headache, or body aches.

diseases.name: Mouth cancer
diseases.summary: Mouth cancer begins in the flat cells lining the lips and mouth and can form a growth that often spreads to neck lymph nodes. It is most often diagnosed in people around age 63, though it can affect anyone. Persistent sores and white or red patches are among its earliest visible signs, and early detection greatly improves the chance of cure.

diseases.name: Movement disorders
diseases.summary: A group of nervous system disorders can disrupt how the body moves, either producing extra unwanted motions or making movement slow and reduced. Some movements happen without the person meaning to make them, and the exact pattern varies widely between subtypes. Many cases can be eased with medicines, physical therapies, or in some situations surgery, and fixing an underlying cause may also help.

diseases.name: Moyamoya disease
diseases.summary: Moyamoya is a rare, slowly progressing condition in which the main arteries supplying the brain narrow or close, so less blood reaches it and the body forms fragile backup vessels. This can cause mini-strokes, strokes, or bleeding in the brain, and it is seen mostly in children and in people of East Asian ancestry. Any sudden neurologic symptom warrants emergency evaluation.

diseases.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia, type 1 (MEN 1)
diseases.summary: A rare inherited disorder in which tumors form in hormone-producing glands, most often the parathyroid, pancreas, and pituitary, though these growths are usually benign. Because the affected glands can overproduce hormones, the condition can produce a range of symptoms, including fatigue, bone problems, kidney stones, and digestive complaints. It cannot be cured, but routine screening allows problems to be found early and treated.

diseases.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia, type 2 (MEN 2)
diseases.summary: A rare inherited disorder that leads to growths in several hormone-producing glands, including the thyroid, adrenal glands, and sometimes the parathyroids. The type known as 2B also tends to produce noticeable bumps on the lips, tongue, and eyes, along with a characteristic tall, slender build. Because it runs in families, relatives of affected people are often screened.

diseases.name: Multiple myeloma
diseases.summary: A cancer of the antibody-producing cells in the bone marrow that can cause bone damage, anemia-like tiredness, and kidney strain from abnormal proteins. Many people have no early signs, and symptoms often appear as bone pain, fractures, infections, or raised blood calcium. It is usually diagnosed in older adults and is more common in men and in Black people in the United States.

diseases.name: Multiple sclerosis
diseases.summary: Multiple sclerosis is a long-term condition in which the immune system damages the insulating coating around nerve fibers in the brain, optic nerve, and spinal cord, which disrupts signal transmission. Symptoms differ widely between people, can shift over time, and often first appear in early adulthood. Anyone with new neurological symptoms should get a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Multiple system atrophy
diseases.summary: A rare, progressive nervous system disorder that impairs movement, balance, speech, and automatic body functions like blood pressure and bladder control. Its signs can resemble Parkinson's disease, though it usually begins in middle age and has no cure, worsening over time.

diseases.name: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) and COVID-19
aliases: COVID-19-associated multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children
diseases.summary: A rare but dangerous immune overreaction that can follow a COVID-19 infection in children, where inflammation damages several organs. It usually shows up within a couple of months of exposure and most often affects school-aged kids. Because it can worsen quickly, any child with these signs needs prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Muscle cramp
diseases.summary: Sudden involuntary tightening of muscles, most often in the calf, that typically passes within moments. Exertion, heat, certain drugs, and some illnesses can bring them on, and the affected area may stay tender afterward. Most cases clear up with home care, but medical review is warranted if they are severe, recurrent, or accompanied by swelling, skin changes, or weakness.

diseases.name: Muscle strains
diseases.summary: A muscle strain is damage to a muscle or the tendon connecting it to bone, ranging from overstretched fibers to a partial or full tear. It is commonly called a pulled muscle and often affects the lower back and back of the thigh. Most mild cases can be handled at home, while serious tears may need medical care.

diseases.name: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS)
diseases.summary: A long-lasting, complex illness marked by profound tiredness that gets worse after physical or mental exertion and is not relieved by rest. Its cause is not known, no single test confirms it, and care focuses on managing symptoms. It is diagnosed after other conditions with similar features have been excluded.

diseases.name: Myasthenia gravis
diseases.summary: A long-term autoimmune disorder that interferes with the signals telling skeletal muscles to contract, leading to weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest. Eye, face, throat, and neck muscles are often affected first, and symptoms can fluctuate in severity over time. It has no cure, but treatment can keep symptoms under control.

diseases.name: Mycosis fungoides
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer of the immune system's T cells that first shows up in the skin, where it can look like eczema or psoriasis and may fade and return for a long time before becoming more serious. It grows slowly, but over time it can thicken into raised patches, form lumps, and in some cases spread to lymph nodes or organs. Because early patches are easy to mistake for common skin conditions, a specialist evaluation is often needed to confirm it.

diseases.name: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD)
diseases.summary: An uncommon-to-rare autoimmune disorder in which the body's defenses mistakenly target the protective myelin coating of nerves in the eyes, brain, and spinal cord. Episodes can come on over days and often leave lasting disability, though they can also occur once and not return. It is more often seen in children and young adults and sometimes follows an infection or vaccine.

diseases.name: Myelodysplastic syndromes
diseases.summary: This blood-forming bone marrow disorder causes blood cells to be made poorly or to function abnormally, and it often produces no noticeable signs at first. As it progresses, it typically leads to tiredness, breathlessness, pale skin, easy bruising, and frequent infections. It mostly affects people over 60 and can follow prior chemotherapy, radiation, or exposure to chemicals such as benzene.

diseases.name: Myelofibrosis
diseases.summary: A chronic blood cancer in which the marrow inside the bones turns fibrous, weakening its ability to produce normal blood cells. It can arise on its own or follow another blood disorder, and some people have no noticeable problems. Care for those with more advanced disease centers on managing their discomfort.

diseases.name: Myocardial bridge
diseases.summary: A myocardial bridge is a artery that runs through a band of heart muscle rather than along its surface, which is present from birth. Most people never notice it, and it is often discovered by accident during imaging done for another reason. When the muscle squeezes the artery hard enough to limit blood flow, typically during exertion, chest discomfort or palpitations can appear.

diseases.name: Myocarditis
diseases.summary: Myocarditis is swelling and irritation of the heart's muscular wall, which can weaken the heart's pumping ability. It is often triggered by a viral infection, though medications or whole-body inflammatory conditions can also be responsible. Some people have no noticeable signs early on, while others develop chest discomfort, breathlessness, or an irregular heartbeat.

diseases.name: Myoclonus
diseases.summary: This is a brief involuntary muscle jerk that can happen in healthy people, such as the jolt right before drifting off to sleep or hiccups. In other cases it signals an underlying neurological, metabolic, or medication-related problem. Most episodes are harmless, but frequent or persistent jerking warrants a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Myofascial pain syndrome
diseases.summary: A long-lasting pain disorder in which tight, sensitive knots within muscles and their surrounding connective sheath cause aching that can spread to distant areas. It often follows repetitive strain, stress-driven muscle clenching, poor posture, or injury, and it persists rather than resolving with rest. Care usually combines exercise, massage, physical therapy, and sometimes targeted injections with pain relief and relaxation techniques.

diseases.name: Myxofibrosarcoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare, slow-growing cancer of the body's supportive connective tissue, most often appearing in the limbs of older adults. It usually shows up as a lump that is not painful. Because it can spread into nearby healthy tissue, any new or changing lump deserves a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Nail fungus
diseases.summary: A widespread fungal infection of the nail that usually begins as a pale or yellowish patch near the tip and slowly changes the nail's color, thickness, and shape. It shows up more often in toenails than fingernails. Mild cases may not need treatment, but the infection often returns even after it has been cleared.

diseases.name: Narcissistic personality disorder
diseases.summary: This is a personality condition in which a person holds an inflated opinion of their own worth and craves praise, yet struggles to feel for others and is easily wounded by criticism. It often strains relationships, job performance, and money management. Those affected rarely seek help on their own, and talk-based therapy is the main approach to treatment.

diseases.name: Narcolepsy
diseases.summary: Narcolepsy is a lifelong brain sleep disorder that causes overwhelming daytime drowsiness and sudden dozing, and it has no cure. Many people also experience episodes of sudden muscle weakness triggered by strong emotions, though medication and lifestyle changes can make it manageable. It typically starts between the ages of 10 and 30 and is strongly linked to family history.

diseases.name: Nasal and paranasal tumors
diseases.summary: Abnormal growths can form inside the nose or in the hollow air spaces around it, and they may be harmless or cancerous. Even harmless growths can physically block breathing through the nose, while cancerous ones can invade nearby tissue and eventually travel elsewhere in the body. Tobacco smoke, polluted air, certain workplace dusts and fumes, and a particular viral infection are linked to a higher chance of developing them.

diseases.name: Nasal polyps
diseases.summary: Nasal polyps are benign, painless lumps that form in the nasal passages and sinus cavities, often appearing in clusters. They tend to develop alongside long-lasting swelling of the sinuses. Larger or numerous growths can obstruct breathing and dull smell, and while medication or surgery can address them, they frequently return.

diseases.name: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma
