It typically comes on quickly and can cause intense itching, widespread reddening and scaling of the skin, and enlarged lymph nodes. Although it cannot be fully cured, treatments can ease symptoms and slow progression.

diseases.name: Shaken baby syndrome
diseases.summary: A forceful shaking of an infant or toddler can injure the brain and, in some cases, cause lasting damage or death. Signs may be subtle, with no visible outer injuries, and children can seem fine at first before developing problems later. Seeking emergency care immediately is critical if violent shaking is suspected.

diseases.name: Shellfish allergy
diseases.summary: A shellfish allergy is an overreaction of the immune system to proteins found in crustaceans and mollusks such as shrimp, crab, oysters, and squid. It is one of the most frequent food allergies in adults, and reactions can range from mild skin or nasal symptoms to life-threatening breathing trouble. Anyone suspecting this allergy should consult a doctor, who can run tests to confirm it.

diseases.name: Shigella infection
diseases.summary: This is a bacterial bowel infection that spreads when traces of an infected person's stool reach the mouth, through hands, contaminated surfaces, food, or water. It mainly causes diarrhea, sometimes with blood, along with cramping and fever. Young children are affected most often, but anyone can catch it, and most episodes ease within about a week, though serious cases may need antibiotics.

diseases.name: Short bowel syndrome
diseases.summary: This digestive disorder arises when the intestine is too short or has lost much of its absorptive surface, so the body cannot take in enough nutrients from food. Symptoms often include chronic loose stools and weight loss, and in children it can slow growth. Treatment focuses on nutritional support, which may include intravenous or tube feeding, dietary changes, and sometimes surgery.

diseases.name: Sjogren disease
diseases.summary: Sjogren disease is a long-term immune condition in which the body mistakenly attacks the moisture-producing glands, mainly around the eyes and mouth. It is diagnosed most often after age 40 and is much more frequent in women. Care centers on relieving symptoms, and it sometimes occurs alongside rheumatoid arthritis or lupus.

diseases.name: Skin cancer
diseases.summary: Abnormal growths on the skin can turn cancerous, most often on areas that see a lot of sun. Most forms are treatable when found early, but melanoma can spread quickly, so changes in a spot or mole are worth having checked promptly.

diseases.name: Skull base tumors
diseases.summary: Skull base tumors are growths forming in the bony floor of the skull, near the eyes, nose, and brain stem, and they can be benign or cancerous. Many cause no noticeable problems, but those that press on nearby nerves, vessels, or brain tissue can disturb vision, hearing, balance, or swallowing. Anyone with worrying symptoms in this area should see a doctor for evaluation.

diseases.name: Sleep apnea
diseases.summary: A sleep-related breathing disorder in which airflow repeatedly drops or halts overnight, often without the person realizing it. It comes in obstructive, central, and mixed forms, and untreated cases can strain the heart over time. Many people only notice the problem when a bed partner reports loud snoring or pauses in breathing, or when daytime exhaustion and poor concentration persist.

diseases.name: Sleep disorders
diseases.summary: A group of nighttime disorders that disturb sleep quality or timing, leaving people tired during the day or causing abnormal breathing or movements while asleep. They can make driving and work less safe and may contribute to other health problems, but they are often treatable.

diseases.name: Sleep terrors (night terrors)
diseases.summary: Sleep terrors cause a sudden episode of screaming, crying, and fear while the person is still asleep, often with flailing limbs and a racing heartbeat. They are most typical in young children and usually fade by the teenage years. Adults can have them too, but far less often.

diseases.name: Sleepwalking
diseases.summary: Sleepwalking is a sleep behavior in which a person gets up and moves around without being fully awake, most often early in the night and most often in children. Occasional episodes are usually harmless and fade on their own, but frequent episodes can point to another sleep problem or a medical issue. Because of the injury risk, households with a sleepwalker should take steps to make the home safer.

diseases.name: Small bowel cancer
diseases.summary: A cancer that begins in the small intestine, the long segment linking the stomach to the large bowel. It often shows up as digestive trouble, jaundice, or unexplained weight loss, and surgery is the usual first treatment.

diseases.name: Small bowel prolapse (enterocele)
diseases.summary: A condition where the upper part of the intestine drops into the lower pelvis and pushes against the top of the vagina, forming a bulge. It happens when the supporting muscles and tissues weaken, often after childbirth or with age. Many people have mild cases with no symptoms, while larger ones can cause pelvic pressure and discomfort, and treatment is often nonsurgical at first.

diseases.name: Small lymphocytic lymphoma
diseases.summary: This is a slow-growing blood cancer that starts in white blood cells called lymphocytes and typically shows up as enlarged lymph nodes. Many people go a long time without needing treatment, and it is usually managed rather than fully cured. Symptoms often appear late or not at all, so a doctor usually finds it through swollen nodes or routine blood work.

diseases.name: Smallpox
diseases.summary: Smallpox is a highly contagious and often fatal viral illness that was eradicated worldwide by 1980 through vaccination, with the last known case in 1977. Its natural presence has ended, though labs retain samples, which keeps concern about deliberate misuse alive. Survivors could be left with permanent facial and body scarring.

diseases.name: Smoldering multiple myeloma (SMM)
diseases.summary: Smoldering multiple myeloma is an early, non-active stage of a blood cancer in which abnormal plasma cells accumulate in the bone marrow and produce an atypical protein. It does not yet cause the organ damage that defines active disease, and many people with it never progress. Monitoring helps separate low-risk cases from higher-risk ones that are more likely to become active myeloma.

diseases.name: Snoring
diseases.summary: Snoring is a rough noise made when relaxed throat tissues shake as air moves through them during sleep. Most people snore occasionally, but frequent or loud snoring can point to obstructive sleep apnea, where breathing repeatedly stalls at night. Lifestyle adjustments often help, and a doctor should be consulted if snoring comes with daytime exhaustion or breathing pauses.

diseases.name: Social anxiety disorder (social phobia)
diseases.summary: Social anxiety disorder is a lasting condition in which ordinary interactions with other people trigger strong unease and worry about being judged or embarrassing oneself. The resulting avoidance can gradually shrink a person's work, school and relationships. Talk-based therapy and medication can help people feel more comfortable around others.

diseases.name: Soft palate cancer
diseases.summary: This is a cancer that begins in the flat cells lining the soft palate, the roof of the back of the mouth, and it is usually a squamous cell carcinoma. It often shows up as a sore or lump that doesn't heal, and it is typically handled with a mix of surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy. It is considered a form of throat cancer and is strongly tied to tobacco, heavy alcohol use, and HPV.

diseases.name: Soft tissue sarcoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer arising in connective and supportive body tissues such as muscle, fat, and nerves, most often in the limbs or abdomen. It often produces no early signs, and the typical first clue is a lump that may not hurt. Outlook varies widely by subtype and stage, with less aggressive tumors that have not spread generally doing better.

diseases.name: Somatic symptom disorder
diseases.summary: A condition where a person fixates on physical sensations to the point that worry, distress, and avoidance disrupt daily life, even when medical tests find nothing serious. Symptoms can be pain, fatigue, or breathlessness, and the intensity of the reaction matters more than the specific complaint. Evaluation by a clinician followed by mental health support usually helps.

diseases.name: Specific phobias
diseases.summary: An intense, persistent fear of a particular object or situation that poses little real danger can dominate a person's choices and disrupt work, school, and social life. The fear typically begins in childhood, runs in families, and is often shaped by a distressing experience or by watching others react. Several effective therapies can help most people overcome it, and earlier treatment tends to work better.

diseases.name: Spina bifida
diseases.summary: This is a birth defect in which the spine and the spinal cord fail to close completely during early pregnancy. Severity varies widely: some people have only a small, hidden gap in the back bones, while others have nerve damage that affects the legs, bladder, and bowels. The most serious forms need surgery soon after birth and lifelong specialist follow-up.

diseases.name: Spinal arteriovenous malformation (AVM)
diseases.summary: A spinal AVM is an abnormal knot of blood vessels on or inside the spinal cord where arteries feed straight into veins, bypassing the normal capillary network. This can starve spinal tissue of oxygen and may cause bleeding or pressure on the cord. Many affected people have few or no signs for years, while others develop leg weakness, numbness, or bladder and bowel trouble.

diseases.name: Spinal cord injury
diseases.summary: Damage to the spinal cord disrupts the signals passing between the brain and the body, often leaving lasting loss of movement, feeling, and bodily control below the injury. The severity and location determine how much function is lost and what recovery is possible. Anyone with a suspected head or neck injury should be treated as having a spinal injury and get emergency care right away.

diseases.name: Spinal cord tumor
diseases.summary: A growth of cells forming in or around the spinal cord, most of which are non-cancerous, though some are malignant. Symptoms often start near the tumor as back or neck pain and can spread to nerve-related problems like weakness, numbness, or bladder and bowel changes as the growth presses on nerves. Anyone with persistent or worrying back pain and neurological changes should see a doctor.

diseases.name: Spinal headaches
diseases.summary: A headache that appears after a spinal tap or spinal anesthesia, usually because fluid slips out through the tiny opening left in the membrane around the spinal cord. It tends to ease when lying flat and worsen when upright, and it often clears up without treatment, though long-lasting cases may need care.

diseases.name: Spinal hemangioma
diseases.summary: This is a non-cancerous growth of abnormal blood vessels inside a vertebra of the spine. Most people never notice it, and it is often found by chance on a scan done for another reason. When it does cause problems, they tend to involve back or neck discomfort and nerve-related changes in the limbs, bladder, or bowels.

diseases.name: Spinal stenosis
diseases.summary: This condition is a narrowing of the spinal canal that can squeeze the spinal cord or nearby nerves. Many people never notice it, but when it causes trouble it often brings leg or arm symptoms that build gradually. It is most often seen in people over 50 and is closely tied to age-related joint wear.

diseases.name: Spinal tumor and spinal mass
diseases.summary: Growths in or around the spinal column, including the bones, cord, and nerve roots, are uncommon, and most spread in from cancers elsewhere in the body. Their most typical sign is back or neck pain that persists, often worse at night or while lying down, and it can spread into limbs or be accompanied by numbness, weakness, or walking difficulty. Anyone with unexplained back pain that lasts weeks or steadily worsens should get it evaluated promptly.

diseases.name: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD)
diseases.summary: A tear inside a heart artery wall lets blood seep between the layers, which can narrow or block the vessel and starve the heart muscle of oxygen. It often strikes people without typical heart disease risks, and it can be fatal if not treated immediately. Any chest discomfort suggesting a heart attack needs emergency care right away.

diseases.name: Sprained ankle
diseases.summary: An ankle sprain is an injury where the tough tissues connecting the ankle bones get overstretched or torn, usually after a twist or roll. Most cases heal with rest and early care, though a clinician should check the ankle to rule out a more serious ligament tear or fracture.

diseases.name: Sprains
diseases.summary: Ligaments are the tough tissue bands holding joints together, and a sprain happens when they get stretched or torn, most often at the ankle after a roll or twist. Most mild cases heal at home with rest, ice, compression and elevation, but more serious tears can need medical care or surgery. Seeing a doctor is important if the joint won't bear weight, there is numbness, or pain sits over the bone.

diseases.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
diseases.summary: A cancer that begins in the flat cells forming the upper layers of the skin, most often on areas that get a lot of sun. It is usually slow-growing and rarely deadly, but it can enlarge or spread if left untreated. Persistent sores that do not heal are the main warning sign.

diseases.name: Stage 4 (metastatic) colon cancer
diseases.summary: Advanced colon cancer that has moved beyond the bowel can show up through changes in digestion, unexplained weight loss, and problems in whichever organ it has reached, such as the liver or lungs. Many people have few or no signs early on, so symptoms can be subtle. Anyone with worrying changes, especially a history of colon cancer, should see a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Stomach cancer
diseases.summary: Stomach cancer, also known as gastric cancer, most often starts where the esophagus joins the stomach and is more frequently found in older adults. Early disease often produces no clear signs, and when symptoms do appear they tend to be vague stomach complaints that are usually caused by something else. Anyone with persistent digestive symptoms or unexplained weight loss should get checked by a doctor.

diseases.name: Stress incontinence
diseases.summary: Stress incontinence is a form of bladder leakage triggered by physical pressure on the bladder, such as coughing, sneezing, or lifting. It is distinct from urge-related leakage and is more likely with age, extra body weight, and, in women, vaginal childbirth. Symptoms often appear only during certain activities and may prompt a visit to a clinician when they interfere with daily life.

diseases.name: Stroke
diseases.summary: A stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is interrupted, either by a blocked vessel or by a vessel that leaks or ruptures. Quick recognition and emergency treatment greatly improve the chances of avoiding lasting brain injury. Typical warning signs involve sudden changes in speech, facial or limb weakness, vision, balance, and headache.

diseases.name: Stuttering
diseases.summary: Stuttering is a speech disorder in which the normal flow and rhythm of talking are repeatedly broken, so a person knows what they want to say but struggles to get the words out. It is especially common in young children learning to talk, and while many outgrow it, it can persist into adulthood and affect confidence and communication. Speech therapy, fluency-enhancing devices, and cognitive behavioral therapy can help.

diseases.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
diseases.summary: Bleeding into the thin layer of space around the brain is a dangerous type of stroke, most often caused by a burst weak spot in a blood vessel. It usually announces itself with an abrupt, extremely intense headache, and it can become life-threatening or cause lasting brain injury without prompt treatment.

diseases.name: Sudden cardiac arrest
diseases.summary: A sudden electrical malfunction in the heart stops it from pumping blood, so the person collapses, loses consciousness, and stops breathing within moments. Unlike a heart attack, which is caused by a blocked vessel, this can occur without warning, though a heart attack can trigger it. Immediate CPR and defibrillation give many people a real chance of survival.

diseases.name: Suicide and suicidal thoughts
diseases.summary: Suicidal thoughts are a sign of intense distress that can often be eased with timely support and professional treatment. Warning signs can be spoken or quiet, and recognizing them early gives people a real chance to get help. Anyone in crisis can reach a free, confidential crisis line at any hour, and emergency services are the right call if immediate danger is present.

diseases.name: Sun allergy
diseases.summary: A skin reaction that appears after UV exposure, most often on areas like the neck and chest, is the most typical form of this condition. It can be hereditary, triggered by medications or skin products, or have no clear cause. Mild cases often fade on their own, while severe ones may need prescription creams or tablets.

diseases.name: Sunburn
diseases.summary: A sunburn is a painful, heated patch of skin that typically shows up a few hours after too much sun exposure. Most cases settle with home care like cooling the skin and over-the-counter pain relief, though full fading can take several days. Protecting skin from UV light all year, including on cloudy days, is the best way to avoid it.

diseases.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
diseases.summary: A fast, out-of-rhythm heart condition that starts in the upper part of the heart. Episodes can come and go over minutes to days, and many people never notice any symptoms. Most cases are manageable, but anyone with heart disease or a prolonged episode needs prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Suspicious breast lumps
diseases.summary: Breast lumps are usually not cancerous, but any new, firm, fixed, or changing lump should be checked by a clinician promptly. Hormonal cycles, pregnancy, and age-related benign conditions are common reasons for lumps, yet skin, nipple, or armpit changes warrant timely evaluation. Persistent lumps lasting more than a few weeks justify an appointment.

diseases.name: Swimmer's itch
diseases.summary: Swimmer's itch is a skin reaction that follows contact with water carrying tiny organisms that briefly enter the skin and then die off. The resulting rash is itchy and typically clears up by itself within a few days. Anti-itch treatments can make the discomfort more manageable while it resolves.

diseases.name: Synovial sarcoma
diseases.summary: A rare soft tissue cancer that usually starts near large joints such as the knee and typically appears in teenagers and young adults. It most often shows up as a slowly growing, often painless lump, sometimes with stiffness or swelling nearby. When it develops in the head or neck, it can also interfere with breathing, swallowing, or voice.

diseases.name: Syphilis
diseases.summary: Syphilis is a bacterial infection passed mainly through sexual contact, and it can also spread from a pregnant person to the baby. It often begins with a painless sore, followed by a rash and flu-like symptoms, and it can stay silent for years before causing serious damage if left untreated. Early infection is usually curable with penicillin, so prompt testing matters.

diseases.name: Syringomyelia
diseases.summary: A slowly progressing fluid-filled cyst forms inside the spinal cord and can expand over time, injuring nerve tissue. Symptoms often appear in adulthood, typically between the mid-twenties and forties, and frequently follow a cape-like pattern across the upper body. Management ranges from monitoring to surgery depending on how troublesome the symptoms become.

diseases.name: Systemic mastocytosis
diseases.summary: This is a rare disorder in which the body accumulates an excess of mast cells, mainly in the skin and bone marrow, and sometimes in the gut, liver, or spleen. When these cells are activated they release histamine and similar chemicals, producing allergy-like reactions. Common provocations include insect stings, alcohol, stress, temperature shifts, physical exertion, and some medications.

diseases.name: T-cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: T-cell lymphomas are a group of blood cancers that begin in a type of white blood cell that helps the body fight germs. They can show up in lymph nodes or in organs such as the skin, gut, or liver, and many people have no symptoms at first. Common warning signs are swollen glands, fever, night sweats, tiredness, and unplanned weight loss.

diseases.name: Tachycardia
diseases.summary: A heart that beats faster than normal can come from many different rhythm disturbances, with a resting rate above 100 per minute usually counting as too fast. Many people feel nothing, while others notice pounding, fluttering, or lightheadedness. Often the cause is harmless, but some forms can progress to serious events, so chest pain, fainting, or breathlessness need prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Tapeworm infection
diseases.summary: A tapeworm can take up residence in the gut, where it often causes little or no trouble, though some people develop stomach upset and diarrhea. When its larval stage forms cysts in the brain, liver, lungs, heart, or eyes, the effects can be serious and depend on the organ involved. Infection is usually linked to eating undercooked meat or fish, and it is treated with antiparasitic medication, sometimes with surgical removal of cysts.

diseases.name: Tay-Sachs disease
diseases.summary: A rare inherited condition in which a missing enzyme lets fatty compounds accumulate in nerve cells, mainly in the brain and spinal cord. The most severe form appears in infancy and usually shortens life to a few years, while juvenile and adult-onset forms progress more slowly. Genetic testing and counseling are recommended for families with a known history or higher-risk ancestry.

diseases.name: Teen depression
diseases.summary: Teen depression is a persistent low mood that goes beyond ordinary teenage ups and downs and disrupts school, home, and friendships. It can show up as emotional shifts like irritability or hopelessness along with changes in sleep, appetite, and energy. Most teens improve with a combination of medication and counseling, but it should be taken seriously and evaluated by a professional.

diseases.name: Teeth grinding (bruxism)
diseases.summary: Bruxism is a common habit of clenching or grinding the teeth, which happens either while awake or during sleep, often without the person realizing it. Over time it can wear teeth down and cause jaw, face, or headache discomfort, and it is frequently linked to stress and sleep problems. Most people see a dentist for it, and children often outgrow it.

diseases.name: Temporal lobe seizure
diseases.summary: A temporal lobe seizure starts in the brain's temporal regions, which handle emotion and short-term memory, so it can change how a person feels and thinks during an episode. Some people notice a warning sensation beforehand, while others stay unaware and appear dazed with repetitive movements. Recovery is often followed by confusion, sleepiness, or gaps in memory.

diseases.name: TEN
diseases.summary: A rare but potentially fatal reaction in which the skin and the moist linings of the mouth, eyes, and genitals break down, most often after a drug exposure. It sits at the severe end of the same spectrum as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and always requires hospital care, with recovery lasting weeks to months.

diseases.name: Tendinitis
diseases.summary: Tendinitis is an irritated, inflamed tendon, the tough cord linking muscle to bone, usually from repeated strain or overuse. It typically produces a dull ache and tenderness near a joint, most often at the shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, or heels. Rest, pain relief, and physical therapy resolve most cases, though long-standing inflammation can eventually lead to a tear.

diseases.name: Tendinopathy
diseases.summary: Tendinopathy is an umbrella term for problems in a tendon, the cord connecting muscle to bone, and it covers inflammation, gradual breakdown, and sheath inflammation. It usually comes from repetitive strain or overuse and most often affects the shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and heels. Most cases improve with rest, physical therapy, and pain relief, and a doctor should be seen if symptoms persist for several days or interfere with daily life.

diseases.name: Tennis elbow
diseases.summary: A common overuse problem where the tendons on the outer side of the elbow become irritated and gradually break down, causing pain that can radiate down into the forearm and wrist. It is most often linked to repetitive arm and wrist movements, and frequently has no obvious single cause. Symptoms usually ease with rest and conservative care, though a doctor should be consulted if self-care does not help.

diseases.name: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor
diseases.summary: This is a rare, usually non-cancerous growth that arises from the lining cells of joints, tendon sheaths, and fluid cushions around joints. It appears in two forms: a slow-growing lump often in the fingers or hand, and a more widespread form that affects large joints like the knee, hip, or ankle and can gradually damage them. It mostly shows up in adults in their thirties to fifties and is seen more often in women.

diseases.name: Tension headache
diseases.summary: A tension-type headache is the most frequent kind of headache, typically producing a dull, pressing discomfort that many people describe as a snug band around the skull. Its exact triggers are unclear, but it often responds to a mix of self-care habits, over-the-counter medication, and other therapies. Medical attention is advisable if pain medicine is needed often or if the headache pattern shifts.

diseases.name: Testicular cancer
diseases.summary: Testicular cancer is a growth of cells beginning in the testicles, which are located in the scrotum, and it most often affects men between about 15 and 45 years old. It usually shows up first as a lump or swelling in one testicle and is highly treatable, even after it has spread, with surgery and chemotherapy as common options. Anyone noticing testicle or groin symptoms that persist beyond two weeks should see a health care provider.

diseases.name: Tetanus
diseases.summary: Tetanus is a bacterial infection in which a toxin makes muscles tighten into painful, uncontrolled contractions, often beginning around the jaw. Symptoms typically emerge one to three weeks after a contaminated wound and can intensify over about two weeks. Because the spasms can interfere with breathing and the illness can be fatal, anyone showing signs needs emergency care, and vaccination remains the main protection.

diseases.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
diseases.summary: A heart defect present from birth that mixes oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood, so less oxygen reaches the body. Infants often look bluish or gray and struggle to feed or breathe, and it is usually found in the first months of life, though milder cases can go unnoticed until adulthood. It requires corrective surgery and lifelong follow-up.

diseases.name: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
diseases.summary: A thoracic aortic aneurysm is a bulge that forms when the wall of the chest portion of the body's largest artery weakens and widens. Most people feel nothing for a long time, and the condition is often found by chance. Warning signs usually appear only as it grows or when it tears or bursts, which is a life-threatening emergency.

diseases.name: Thoracic outlet syndrome
diseases.summary: Thoracic outlet syndrome happens when the nerves or blood vessels that run through the narrow gap between the collarbone and the first rib get pinched or irritated. Which symptoms appear depends on whether nerves, veins, or arteries are the ones affected, so the experience differs widely between people. Symptoms often flare with overhead arm movement, and most cases are not an emergency, though sudden swelling, color change, or a weak cold hand needs immediate care.

diseases.name: Throat cancer
diseases.summary: This is a cancer that begins in the throat, a muscular tube running from behind the nose down to the neck, and it can also begin in the voice box. Where it starts determines which symptoms show up, so signs range from a persistent sore throat and ear pain to hoarseness and blood when coughing. Tobacco, heavy drinking, certain viral infections such as HPV, and low fruit and vegetable intake raise the chance of developing it.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia (low platelet count)
diseases.summary: A condition where the blood carries fewer than normal platelets, the small cells that help stop bleeding. It often causes no problems when mild, but a low count can lead to easy bruising, tiny spots on the skin, and prolonged bleeding after minor injuries. Persistent or uncontrolled bleeding needs prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Thrombocytosis
diseases.summary: Thrombocytosis means the bone marrow makes more clotting cell fragments than needed, usually as a response to another illness, inflammation, or low red blood cell count, though sometimes no cause is found. Many affected people feel nothing at all, and the condition is often picked up incidentally on a routine blood count. When symptoms do appear, they tend to reflect clotting problems, and very high counts can occasionally cause bleeding.

diseases.name: Thumb arthritis
diseases.summary: Thumb arthritis is a wearing down of the protective lining at the joint where the thumb meets the wrist, and it becomes more likely with age. It typically brings aching at the base of the thumb, especially during gripping or pinching, along with reduced hand strength. Persistent symptoms in this area are worth having checked by a clinician.

diseases.name: Thunderclap headaches
diseases.summary: A sudden, extremely intense head pain that reaches its maximum within a minute, often with nausea or vomiting. It is uncommon, but it can signal a dangerous bleeding problem in or around the brain, so it requires emergency evaluation.

diseases.name: Thyroid cancer
diseases.summary: Thyroid cancer starts when cells in the butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck begin dividing uncontrollably and form a growth. Many cases cause no noticeable signs at first, and it often appears as a lump in the neck or changes in voice or swallowing as it grows. Most cases are very treatable, and the outlook is generally good.

diseases.name: Tinnitus
diseases.summary: Tinnitus is the perception of sound such as ringing or buzzing when no external source exists, so typically only the person hearing it can notice it. It is quite widespread, touching a sizable share of adults, and it tends to appear more often with advancing age. Often it eases once whatever underlying problem is addressed, and various approaches can make it less intrusive.

diseases.name: TMJ disorders
diseases.summary: Temporomandibular joint disorders cause pain and tenderness in the hinge connecting the lower jaw to the skull, along with the muscles that move it. The underlying trigger is often unclear and tends to reflect a combination of habits like teeth grinding, stress, and related conditions such as arthritis or fibromyalgia. Many cases settle on their own or improve with home care, a night guard, and jaw physiotherapy.

diseases.name: Tongue cancer
diseases.summary: Tongue cancer, usually a squamous cell type, begins as abnormal cell growth on the tongue and can show up either on the visible front part of the tongue or at the back near the throat. Oral cancers tend to produce noticeable signs early, such as a sore that won't heal, while throat-based cancers often stay silent until neck lymph nodes swell. Tobacco and heavy alcohol use are the strongest known risk factors, and any persistent mouth or throat symptom warrants a prompt visit to a clinician.

diseases.name: Tongue-tie (ankyloglossia)
diseases.summary: A condition present from birth in which a short, thick, or tight band under the tongue limits how freely the tongue can move. It can make breastfeeding, eating, or speech harder, though many people with it never have problems. Treatment, when needed, is usually a simple surgical release of the band.

symptoms.name: difficulty moving tongue side to side

diseases.name: Tonic-clonic (grand mal) seizure
diseases.summary: A seizure involving stiffening and then rhythmic jerking of the body, with loss of awareness, is usually tied to epilepsy but can also follow high fever, brain injury, or other medical problems. Most people who have a single episode recover without ongoing treatment, while recurrent episodes call for daily medication and sometimes surgery or diet changes. Any seizure lasting over five minutes, or without prompt recovery of breathing or consciousness, needs emergency help.

diseases.name: Tonsil cancer
diseases.summary: Tonsil cancer is a malignancy beginning in one of the two immune tissue pads at the back of the throat. It often goes unnoticed until it has reached nearby lymph nodes in the neck. Tobacco, heavy alcohol use, and certain HPV infections raise the chance of developing it.

diseases.name: Tourette syndrome
diseases.summary: Tourette syndrome is a neurological condition in which a person makes sudden, repeated movements or noises that are hard to suppress. It usually appears in childhood and often eases in the late teens and adulthood. Treatment is available, but many people with mild cases never need it.

diseases.name: Toxic hepatitis
diseases.summary: A condition where the liver becomes irritated and swollen after contact with a harmful substance such as alcohol, a chemical, a medication, or a supplement. Symptoms may start within hours or appear only after months of exposure, and they usually ease once the substance is avoided. Repeated or heavy exposure can scar the liver or, rarely, cause it to fail.

diseases.name: Toxoplasmosis
diseases.summary: Toxoplasmosis is a widespread parasitic infection usually acquired from undercooked meat or contact with cat feces, and most people never notice it. When symptoms do appear they tend to resemble a mild flu, but the infection can seriously affect the eyes, brain, and lungs of people with weakened immunity and can harm a developing baby. Treatment is typically reserved for severe cases, pregnancy, newborns, and immunocompromised patients.

diseases.name: Tracheomalacia
diseases.summary: A structural weakness in the cartilage of the breathing tube can let the passage narrow during inhalation, coughing, or feeding, most often in infants. The narrowing can make breathing noisy and laborious and raises the chance of repeated lung infections. Many affected babies improve as their airway firms up with age, while more serious cases may need medication, therapy, or surgery.

diseases.name: Trachoma
diseases.summary: This is a contagious bacterial eye infection that spreads through shared secretions and contaminated items, and it is most common where clean water and healthcare are scarce. Early signs are often mild, but repeated infection can scar the eyelids and eventually cause blindness if left untreated. Prompt treatment is the key to preventing lasting damage.

diseases.name: Transient ischemic attack (TIA)
diseases.summary: A temporary episode that mimics a stroke, triggered when blood supply to part of the brain drops for a moment. Symptoms typically fade within an hour and usually leave no lasting injury. Because it can come before a full stroke, it calls for prompt medical assessment.

diseases.name: Transposition of the great arteries
diseases.summary: A birth heart defect in which the two large vessels carrying blood out of the heart are connected to the wrong pumping chambers. Infants often turn blue and struggle to feed or gain weight, and the form that does not switch oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood as quickly can stay hidden for years. Surgical correction is the standard treatment and is usually performed in the first weeks of life.

diseases.name: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM)
diseases.summary: This is a heart disease in which a protein made by the liver becomes misshapen and clumps into deposits inside the heart muscle, making it rigid and hard to fill and pump. Its symptoms overlap with many other heart problems, so it is often overlooked, and the same deposits can also affect nerves and digestion. Newer medications can slow progression, but damage that has already occurred may be permanent.

diseases.name: Traveler's diarrhea
diseases.summary: A bout of gut infection picked up while abroad, typically from tainted food or water, that brings sudden watery bowel movements and cramping. Most cases clear up by themselves within a few days, but people who have high fevers, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration should get medical care.

diseases.name: Trichotillomania (hair-pulling disorder)
diseases.summary: Hair-pulling disorder is a psychological condition in which a person feels repeated, hard-to-resist urges to yank out their own hair, most often from the scalp. It usually starts around the preteen or early teen years and tends to flare and fade over time if left untreated. The visible hair loss and emotional strain it causes often make professional support worthwhile.

diseases.name: Tricuspid valve disease
diseases.summary: The tricuspid valve, which sits between the right upper and lower heart chambers, can leak backward or become narrowed, forcing the heart to work harder to send blood to the lungs and body. Many people with the leaking type feel nothing at all, while others notice tiredness, fluid buildup, or heart rhythm changes. Congenital forms can appear in infancy with bluish skin and poor feeding or growth.

diseases.name: Tricuspid valve regurgitation
diseases.summary: A one-way valve on the right side of the heart fails to seal completely, letting some blood slip in the wrong direction. Mild cases often cause no problems and are found by chance during heart imaging, but significant leakage can strain the right side of the heart. It may be present from birth or develop later from heart rhythm problems, heart attacks, or other heart conditions.

diseases.name: Trigeminal neuralgia
diseases.summary: A nerve disorder on the face that produces brief, violent stabbing pain, often set off by everyday actions like eating, talking, or washing. It mostly affects women and adults over fifty, and while it can recur for a long time, treatment generally keeps it under control.

diseases.name: Trigger finger
diseases.summary: A tendon in a finger struggles to slide through its surrounding sleeve, usually because the sleeve thickens or a small bump forms on the tendon. The finger can catch in a bent position and then snap straight. It is more frequent in women over 50 and in people with diabetes, thyroid problems, or rheumatoid arthritis.

diseases.name: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC)
diseases.summary: This is an aggressive form of breast cancer that lacks the three receptors that many breast cancers use to grow, so hormone-blocking drugs and HER2-targeted treatments do not work for it. It often appears in younger women, is more common in Black women, and is frequently found at a later stage, which is why treatment usually begins with chemotherapy or immunotherapy. Because it can grow quickly between mammograms, any new breast change should be checked by a clinician promptly.

diseases.name: Triple-positive breast cancer
diseases.summary: This form of breast cancer carries receptors for estrogen and progesterone and also produces excess HER2 protein, which is why it is labeled with three positive results. Because of this profile, hormone-blocking drugs and HER2-targeted medicines are options alongside surgery and radiation. Early detection often allows a cure, and even advanced cases can be slowed with treatment.

diseases.name: Truncus arteriosus
diseases.summary: A rare heart defect present from birth in which a single large vessel leaves the heart instead of the usual two, so oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood blend together. Newborns often show low oxygen signs such as bluish skin and fast breathing in their first days, and surgery is the standard fix, most successful when done early.

diseases.name: Tuberous sclerosis
diseases.summary: A genetic condition that leads to noncancerous growths in organs such as the skin, brain, kidneys, heart, lungs, and eyes. Its signs differ widely from person to person and can appear in infancy, childhood, or adulthood, or sometimes not at all. Treatments can ease symptoms, though there is no cure.

diseases.name: Tubular adenoma of the colon
diseases.summary: Tubular adenomas, the most common precancerous growths found during colonoscopy, usually cause no noticeable signs and are typically found during routine screening. When symptoms do appear, they tend to be subtle changes in bowel habits or small amounts of blood in the stool. Because these growths can slowly turn into colon cancer, removal and follow-up colonoscopy are recommended.

diseases.name: Type 1 diabetes
diseases.summary: Type 1 diabetes is a long-term autoimmune condition in which the immune system destroys the insulin-producing cells of the pancreas, leaving the body unable to move blood sugar into its tissues for energy. There is no cure yet, but insulin treatment and careful monitoring can prevent serious complications and let most people maintain a full, active life. It is often first noticed in childhood or adolescence, though it can begin at any age.

diseases.name: Type 1 diabetes in children
diseases.summary: A condition in which a child's immune system destroys the cells that produce insulin, so the body can no longer move blood sugar into cells for energy. It cannot be cured, but daily insulin and blood sugar monitoring allow children to live active lives. Symptoms tend to appear abruptly and warrant prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Type 2 diabetes
diseases.summary: A long-term condition in which the body resists or underuses its blood-sugar-lowering hormone, so glucose accumulates and can gradually harm vessels and organs. It often develops quietly over years and is most typical in middle-aged and older adults, though younger people are increasingly affected. Lifestyle changes can keep it in check, and medication may be needed when they are not enough.

diseases.name: Type 2 diabetes in children
diseases.summary: A slowly developing, long-term metabolic disorder in which a child's body handles blood sugar poorly, so glucose accumulates in the blood. It is increasingly seen in young people because of rising rates of childhood excess weight. Management centers on diet, activity and weight, with medication or insulin needed if lifestyle changes are not enough.

diseases.name: Ulcerative colitis
diseases.summary: Ulcerative colitis is a long-term inflammatory condition that affects the lining of the large bowel and rectum, causing sores and recurring flare-ups. Although it has no cure, it is usually manageable with treatment, and many people can reach long stretches without symptoms. Persistent bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, or unexplained fever warrant prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Ulnar wrist pain
diseases.summary: Discomfort on the pinky-finger edge of the wrist usually comes from a problem with the bones, tendons, or ligaments there, often after an injury. Athletes, people who repeat the same hand motions for work, and people with loose ligaments or arthritis are more prone to it. Grip strength and the ability to turn the forearm or bend the wrist can be affected.

diseases.name: Undescended testicle
diseases.summary: A testicle that fails to drop into the scrotum before birth, most often affecting one side and sometimes both. Many cases correct themselves within the first few months of life, while persistent ones are usually treated with surgery in infancy to lower the chance of later fertility and testicular cancer problems.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS)
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer of the body's connective tissues, such as muscle, fat, and blood vessels, and it usually shows up as a painless-to-painful growing mass in an arm or leg. When it spreads, it most often reaches the lungs, which can cause breathing or chest symptoms. Medical teams typically treat it with a combination of surgery, radiation, and medication, and it is most often diagnosed in adults between about 50 and 70.

diseases.name: Ureteral cancer
diseases.summary: A cancer that forms in the narrow tubes carrying urine from the kidneys to the bladder. It is uncommon overall, mostly affects older adults, and is often found in people with a history of bladder cancer. Blood in the urine and back pain are typical early clues, and anyone with persistent worrying symptoms should see a doctor.

diseases.name: Ureteral obstruction
diseases.summary: A blockage in one or both of the narrow tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder can build up pressure and damage kidney function if left alone. It often causes flank or abdominal pain, changes in urine output, or infection, though some people notice nothing at all. The condition is treatable, but untreated cases can progress quickly to serious complications.

diseases.name: Urethral cancer
diseases.summary: Urethral cancer is an uncommon tumor that forms in the narrow passage linking the bladder to the outside of the body. It affects people of any sex but is seen more often in men, and it becomes more likely with age and with long-term irritation of the urethra. Because symptoms often resemble less serious urinary problems, anyone with ongoing urinary changes or unexplained genital lumps should see a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Urethral stricture
diseases.summary: Scarring can tighten the urine tube running from the bladder to the outside, making it harder for urine to leave fully. This often leads to a weaker, slower stream, a feeling of incomplete emptying, and more frequent urination. Because urine can linger, infections may follow.

diseases.name: Urinary incontinence
diseases.summary: Urinary incontinence means losing control of the bladder, ranging from small leaks when coughing or sneezing to sudden urges that are hard to reach a toilet in time for. It becomes more frequent with age, but it is not an unavoidable part of getting older. Most people improve with lifestyle and diet changes or medical treatment, so seeing a doctor is worthwhile when it disrupts daily life.

diseases.name: Urinary tract infection (UTI)
diseases.summary: An infection in any part of the urinary tract, though it most often settles in the bladder and urethra and causes discomfort when passing urine. If it climbs up to the kidneys it becomes more serious and can bring fever, flank pain, and sickness. Women are affected far more often than men, largely because of their shorter urethra.

diseases.name: Urine color
diseases.summary: Urine can shift to unusual shades for harmless reasons, such as eating certain foods or taking some medicines. A color change that has no dietary or drug explanation may instead reflect a problem in the urinary tract, kidneys, bladder, or liver. A change accompanied by pain, visible blood, or yellowing of the skin and eyes calls for a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Uterine fibroids
diseases.summary: This condition involves noncancerous muscular growths in the uterus that are common during the childbearing years, and many people with them never notice any problems. When they do cause trouble, the effects depend on how many there are, how large they grow, and where they sit within the uterine wall. Heavy or painful periods and pelvic pressure are the usual complaints, while sudden sharp pain or heavy bleeding needs prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Uterine prolapse
diseases.summary: A condition where the womb drops down toward or through the vaginal opening because the surrounding pelvic supports have become lax. It is most often found in women past menopause who have had vaginal births, and mild cases often cause no noticeable problems. Care is typically sought when the symptoms interfere with everyday activities.

diseases.name: Uterine sarcoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer that forms in the muscle or connective tissue of the uterus rather than its lining, and it accounts for only a small share of uterine cancers. Because it arises from different tissue, it can behave differently from the more common endometrial cancers, with some subtypes growing slowly and others spreading quickly. It often causes no symptoms early on, and when symptoms appear they overlap with benign problems like fibroids.

diseases.name: Vaginal agenesis
diseases.summary: Vaginal agenesis is a rare condition present from birth in which the vagina does not fully form, and the uterus may be underdeveloped or missing. It often comes to light in the teen years when a girl has not started her period, and it can be accompanied by kidney, spine, or other developmental differences. Dilator therapy or, occasionally, surgery can create a functional vagina that allows intercourse.

diseases.name: Vaginal cancer
diseases.summary: Cancer arising in the vaginal canal is uncommon, and many cases actually start in another organ and move into the vagina. Early tumors often cause no noticeable problems, but as they enlarge they can produce unusual bleeding, discharge, a palpable lump, or pain in the pelvis and urinary area. Detection while the tumor remains limited to the vagina gives the most favorable prognosis.

diseases.name: Vaginal fistula
diseases.summary: A vaginal fistula is an abnormal passage between the vagina and a nearby organ such as the bladder, ureter, urethra, rectum, colon, or small intestine, often arising after childbirth, injury, surgery, infection, or radiation. Leakage of urine, stool, or gas through the vagina, along with recurrent urinary or vaginal infections, are typical signs. Because it generally needs medical evaluation and often surgical repair, a checkup is advisable when these symptoms appear.

diseases.name: Varicocele
diseases.summary: Varicoceles are swollen veins around the testicle that usually develop during puberty and often cause no trouble at all. When they do cause problems, they can bring on a dull ache, a lump that feels like a bag of worms, or fertility difficulties, and surgery is sometimes advised. Because they are typically harmless, most cases call for a routine doctor visit rather than emergency care.

diseases.name: Varicose veins
diseases.summary: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted vessels just beneath the skin, most often in the legs, that develop when internal valves stop keeping blood moving upward. The condition is often mainly a cosmetic concern, but it can cause aching and discomfort and occasionally leads to more serious problems. Exercise, elevating the legs, and compression stockings often help, and a procedure may be used when those measures are not enough.

diseases.name: Vasculitis
diseases.summary: Vasculitis is a group of mostly uncommon disorders in which the blood vessels become inflamed, and the resulting stiffening and narrowing can starve tissues of blood. Which organs are affected determines the range of signs, and while some forms resolve on their own, most need long-term medication. Because certain types can progress quickly, prompt medical evaluation is important.

diseases.name: Vasovagal syncope
diseases.summary: Vasovagal syncope is a brief fainting episode triggered when the body overreacts to things like blood or strong emotion, causing heart rate and blood pressure to fall suddenly. It is typically harmless, though a fall during a faint can cause injury. Doctors may still check for heart problems, especially after a first episode.

diseases.name: Ventricular tachycardia
diseases.summary: A fast, irregular heartbeat that begins in the heart's lower chambers can reduce blood flow to the body, so organs may not get enough oxygen. Brief episodes are often harmless, but longer ones can cause fainting, cardiac arrest, or sudden death and need emergency evaluation. Heart disease, certain medicines, electrolyte imbalances, and stimulant drug use raise the risk.

diseases.name: Vertebral tumor
diseases.summary: An abnormal mass forming within the vertebrae of the spinal column, which may be harmless or cancerous. Most cancerous cases come from a tumor that began in another organ and traveled to the spine. Early signs often include back pain, and nerve-related symptoms or loss of bladder or bowel control signal the need for urgent care.

diseases.name: Vesicoureteral reflux
diseases.summary: In this condition, urine that has reached the bladder moves backward up the tubes toward the kidneys instead of staying on its one-way route. It is found mostly in infants and young children, and it often comes to light through repeated bladder infections. Some children show no obvious signs, and it can sometimes be spotted by imaging before birth.

diseases.name: VEXAS syndrome
diseases.summary: This is a rare inflammatory disorder that stems from a gene change acquired within the body's cells during a person's lifetime, so it is not passed down to children. It mainly appears in older adults, with men affected more often, and can involve many organ systems at once. Diagnosis depends on genetic testing, and treatment usually relies on medications, with stem cell or chemotherapy options in some cases.

diseases.name: Viral hemorrhagic fevers
diseases.summary: A group of serious infections caused by several different viruses can injure small blood vessels, causing leakage, and interfere with normal clotting. They are mostly found in tropical regions and are usually picked up through travel, contact with infected animals or people, or exposure to infected body fluids. Only a few of these illnesses have approved vaccines or specific treatments, so prevention relies heavily on avoiding exposure.

diseases.name: Viral hepatitis
diseases.summary: Viral hepatitis is liver inflammation caused by one of several hepatotropic viruses, most often types A, B, C, D, or E. Many infected people have no noticeable signs, while others develop fatigue, fever, yellowed skin, or upper-right abdominal discomfort. Sudden jaundice, upper belly tenderness, or confusion signal acute liver failure and call for emergency care.

diseases.name: Vocal cord paralysis
diseases.summary: When the nerves feeding the voice box get interrupted, one or both vocal cords can stop moving properly, which affects speaking, breathing, and swallowing. Surgery on the neck or chest and certain neurological diseases are known to raise the chance of this happening. Because the cords also guard the airway, persistent hoarseness or swallowing trouble should be checked by a clinician.

diseases.name: Voice disorders
diseases.summary: Voice disorders alter how the voice sounds and are often linked to vocal fold problems, nerve or neurological conditions, reflux, or overuse. A hoarse voice that lasts two to four weeks without a cold or respiratory infection warrants an examination by a clinician. Treatment ranges from voice rest and speech therapy to medication, botulinum toxin injections, or surgery, depending on the cause.

diseases.name: Vulvar cancer
diseases.summary: Vulvar cancer is an uncommon malignancy that develops in the external female genital skin. It often appears first as a bump or sore that may itch, and it is most often found in older women, though younger people can develop it. Early detection usually allows a more limited surgical removal.

diseases.name: Vulvodynia
diseases.summary: Vulvodynia is a long-lasting pain or discomfort centered on the outer female genitals, lasting at least three months without an obvious cause. It can make sitting, exercise, and intimacy hard, and it often needs a medical exam to rule out other treatable problems.

diseases.name: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
diseases.summary: This slow-growing blood cancer often causes no noticeable problems for years. When it does, people may feel tired, run a fever, sweat heavily at night, or lose weight without trying. In some cases excess protein in the blood thickens it and causes vision, neurologic, or bleeding problems that need emergency care.

diseases.name: Wet macular degeneration
diseases.summary: This eye disorder involves abnormal blood vessels leaking into the central part of the retina, which drives a rapid decline in the sharp central sight needed for reading and recognizing faces. It is a later form of age-related macular damage that usually develops from an earlier, slower type, and prompt care can sometimes restore lost vision.

diseases.name: Whiplash
diseases.summary: Whiplash is a neck injury caused by a sudden, forceful back-and-forth jolt of the head and neck, often from rear-end car collisions but also from sports contact, assault, or falls. Most people recover within a few weeks with pain relief and exercise, though a minority develop lasting neck pain or other complications. Prompt medical evaluation is advised to rule out fractures or other structural damage.

diseases.name: Wilms tumor
diseases.summary: This childhood kidney cancer, the most frequent of its kind in young patients, usually shows up as a lump or swelling in the belly, often in children around ages three to four. Many affected children have no noticeable signs at all, and when symptoms do appear they are often caused by something other than this tumor. With modern diagnosis and treatment, the outlook for most children is good.

diseases.name: Wilson's disease
diseases.summary: This is a genetic disorder present from birth in which the body cannot clear excess dietary metal, which then settles in the liver, brain, and eyes. Signs typically surface during childhood through early adulthood and can involve movement, mood, the liver, and the skin or nails. Catching it early makes it manageable, so anyone with a family history or unexplained symptoms should be evaluated.

diseases.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome
diseases.summary: This is a heart condition present from birth in which a spare conduction route lets electrical impulses skip the usual relay, producing episodes of racing heartbeat. Many people never notice symptoms and the pattern is often found by chance on a heart tracing. Episodes are typically manageable, but rare serious complications can occur, so doctors may use medication or a procedure to block the spare route.

diseases.name: Wrinkles
diseases.summary: Fine lines and creases develop as skin around the eyes, mouth, neck and hands becomes thinner, drier and less elastic over time. Sun exposure and smoking accelerate this process, while daily sunscreen and quitting smoking can prevent some of it. Several treatments exist for people who find them bothersome, and a dermatologist can help plan care.

diseases.name: Wrist pain
diseases.summary: Wrist pain frequently comes from a sudden injury like a sprain or fracture, but it can also build slowly from repetitive strain, arthritis, or nerve compression. Because many causes look alike, pinpointing the source often takes a clinical exam. Minor cases tend to settle with rest and over-the-counter pain relief, while pain or swelling that persists or worsens warrants a medical visit.

diseases.name: X-linked agammaglobulinemia
diseases.summary: A rare inherited immune disorder in which the body produces very few protective antibodies, so infections become frequent and hard to clear, usually showing up in infancy or toddlerhood. It mostly affects boys because it is passed down through the mother's genes. Treatment centers on regular infusions of antibodies donated by healthy people.

diseases.name: Yeast infection (vaginal)
diseases.summary: A fungal overgrowth in the vagina and vulva that often follows antibiotic use, hormonal shifts, or poorly controlled blood sugar. Most people get it at least once, and it usually causes itching, irritation, and a thick, odorless discharge. Recurrent or severe cases, or those in pregnancy or with weakened immunity, need a doctor's evaluation.

diseases.name: Yips
diseases.summary: The yips cause sudden, involuntary movements in the hands or wrists that tend to strike during precise actions like putting in golf. Current understanding links many cases to a nerve-based movement disorder rather than nerves or pressure alone, and adjusting grip or equipment often eases the problem.

diseases.name: Zenker's diverticulum
diseases.summary: A small sac can develop where the food tube meets the back of the throat. As it enlarges, it can hold onto food, mucus, or pills, which may later come back up or spill toward the airway. Doctors do not know what causes it, it mostly affects older men, and surgery is often needed once symptoms appear.

diseases.name: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
diseases.summary: This is a rare disorder where small growths, usually in the pancreas or upper small intestine, release excess hormone that drives the stomach to make too much acid. The result is painful stomach ulcers along with digestive complaints like diarrhea and weight loss. Treatment centers on acid-reducing medicine, with surgery sometimes needed to remove the growths.
